en: In the Baiyun Chan Records, those throughout the world with rounded heads and square robes—whose traces fill the mountains and valleys—seek the learning to which they have attained.
Some attain it in the mind, while others attain it in words. To attain it in the mind but fail in words is not what is called "attaining the mind. Attaining... [the mind].
If there is a lapse in speech, it is not that the mind has attained [the truth]; these are all cases of being clear regarding one-sidedness while remaining blind to the dual illumination.
As for my teacher, Duan: possessing such transcendent and extraordinary endowment, born amidst the regions of Heng and Xiang, he was able to "mind" with no-mind;
what could there be that could not be centered in the mind? He was able to "speak" with no-speech; what could there be [that he could not express]?
Yet it cannot be fully expressed in words. There are two who serve as his attendants throughout the prefecture: Jiang and Shu.
There are six monasteries where he burns incense and offers prayers: Chengtian, Yuan Tong, Fahua, Longmen, Xinghua, and Haihui.
Since the places where he dwells are so numerous and the accounts thereof are so abundant, his disciple Chu Ning has compiled [this record].

I have bound them into volumes, divided into the sections of Upper, Middle, and Lower. Since I am well aware of the Master’s vast learning and sought to provide these volumes with a title, I have further requested that he compose a preface for them.
Because the Master passed away at Haihui (Sea-Assembly), and the mountain of Haihui is called Baiyun (White Cloud), I have titled the collection as a whole *The Zen Records of Baiyun*.
As for the causes through which he attained the Dharma, these are recorded within the volumes themselves and need not be recounted here. Hereafter—
By inferring his mind from these remaining writings, one knows that the knower is unimpeded by words; by seeking out his words, one knows that the speaker is unimpeded by the mind.
Only then can one believe that he was my primary teacher. This is the preface by Wang Zizhi of Taiyuan.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Baiyun Yuan, Volume One:
Record of the Teachings at Chengtian Chan Monastery in Jiangzhou,
Compiled by the Junior Disciple Chuning.
On the day the Master opened the hall, he ascended the seat and held up the incense, saying: "This one portion of incense is offered for the present Emperor.
We humbly pray that the wind of Yao may forever fan, and the sun of Shun may shine afar. He then held up another portion of incense and said:
"This one portion of incense is offered for all those within the great ocean of awakening—past, present, and future—who have benefited all living beings."

To all the sages and worthies, as well as the various spiritual friends I have encountered throughout my life, my fellow practitioners and dharma brothers within the assembly who have bestowed upon me even a single word or phrase, my teachers and parents, and all those who have shown me kindness—I offer this slight expression of gratitude.

Again, he held up the incense and said: "As for this single portion of incense, tell me, for whom is it intended? If there were some specific purpose, it would be like snow [falling on a heated surface]."
"Adding frost on top of snow. If one does nothing at all, the fault would be greater than that.

On behalf of my late master, who first resided at Yangqi in Yuanzhou and later at Yungai in Tanzhou—a true ancient patriarch who personally encountered Ciming—who would have known that today, right here, he would cast aside three and let go of two?
He then sat down. Master Nuo of Yuan Tong struck the gavel and said: "The Dharma..."
Seated amidst this assembly of dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary truth (*paramārtha*).

The Master then looked to his left and right and said, "If you simply disperse like this, then from antiquity to the present, such people are as numerous as hemp and millet. If you say there is anything more—'how should it be?
or 'what should be done?'—then the single path of Caoxi will sink into oblivion. Therefore, all the sages of the past emerged from within the flames to extend their hands, desiring only this."
All people go about with eyes askance and noses straight. Is there anyone in this assembly today who can let their hands hang down?
Come forth and see! A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does your lineage follow?
The Master said, "One hand cannot clap alone; two hands produce a clear, resonant sound. The monk said, "A true lion cub is able to roar like a lion. The Master said, "I urge you..."
"You, stop! Stop right there! Do not wait for the wind to rise before entering deeper.
A monk asked, "If one wishes to travel a thousand li, the first step is the beginning. What is this very first step? The Master said, "Stand over here.

The monk said, "At the break of dawn, when the night is nearly spent, there are still those traveling in the dark. The Master said, "I do not yet grant you permission. The monk gave a shout. The Master said:
"Eh? A monk asked, "When humans and devas meet, both are able to see one another. What is the matter of this mutual seeing?
The Master said, "How would I dare deceive you? The monk said, "If that is so, then having long endured the hardships of the desert sands, today I have met with true wisdom."
The Master said, "What is the state of your own heels? The monk said, "The myriad waters contain the solitary moon; the host of stars bow to the Northern Dipper.
The Master said, "Li Bai remains, as before, a mere scholar. A monk asked, "The assembly of humans and devas has gathered to listen to the sound of the tide.
As the Lord of the Prefecture presides at this banquet, what matter should he discuss? The Master said, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "In such a manner..."
"If so, then within the nine rivers and a thousand li, every blade of grass and tree receives the grace. The Master said, "This would make the patch-robed monks laugh to death.
A monk took his sitting cloth, gave it a single sweep, and then departed. The Master said, "Vague is the Kingdom of Yue; faint is Yangzhou. He then said:
Let us cease this dialogue. Both question and answer belong to the realm of gain and loss. As the ancients said: "To move is to give rise to the root of birth and death;
to be still is to sink into the land of stupor and intoxication. If both movement and stillness are extinguished, one falls into a void of nihilism;

if both movement and stillness are grasped together, one lands in a vague, muddled Buddha-nature. Reaching this point, even if one exhausts the profound dialectics of heaven and exhausts the pivotal wisdom of the world, it remains but a trace.

The pivot: there is not a single point where it can be grasped. Only this mountain monk, today, having fortunately encountered a world of great peace, travels wherever the path leads, unafraid of the laughter or strangeness of others.
Therefore it is said: "In the realm above, on the side of all Buddhas, not a single hair's breadth has been added;
in the realm below, on the side of all sentient beings, not a single hair's breadth has been subtracted. It is only because of this...
Reflecting on delusion: turning one's back on awakening and uniting with the sensory dust, one revolves through the three realms of suffering without a moment’s rest.

Consequently, our Fundamental Teacher from Zhugan was compelled to stir profound waves from within the great ocean of liberation; outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles, he pointed directly to the human mind.
"Seeing one's nature is attaining Buddhahood. Yet tell me, regarding all this entanglement today, where is the point of direct pointing?
If you seek it within the mouth of an elder, it is much like greedily gazing at the moon in the sky while forgetting the lamp inside the room.
If you try to understand it in a state of silence and non-speaking, even until the entire earth is reached, tongues will be tied and sharp edges blunted; it is simply this: nothingness.
"Kong’s iron hammer—what use is it? Here, is there anyone who understands? After a long silence, he said:
"I see only white clouds scattering away; I do not know whose house the bright moon has fallen upon. (The words of thanks are not recorded.)
The next day, he ascended the hall and said: "Master Xuedou said: 'I have unexpectedly continued the lamp that illuminates the night atop Lingfeng Peak;
I suddenly board an iron boat and descend into the vast ocean. Today, I too shall follow this precedent and board an iron boat. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra..."
Guangzhao took the helm for Chengtian; Guanyin and Mokṣala rowed the oars and steered the rudder for him.
Chengtian simply sat on the ground watching Yangzhou. Since this is so, tell me: with what will you repay everyone?
After a long silence, he said: "Who would have known that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is yet another way of thinking?
He then ascended the hall, clapped his hands, and laughed heartily, saying: "O assembly! Where one finds elegance, let there be elegance!"
Upon arriving at Yuantong’s formal assembly, a monk asked, "When two masters meet, what should they discuss? The Master said, "Six ears do not suit a secret.
The monk said, "Thank you for your answer, Master. The Master said, "You did not hear the matter clearly; you call a bell a jar. The monk gave a shout.
The Master said, "A mistake. He then continued: "When the autumn river is clear and shallow, the white heron blends with the misty isle. How excellent is Avalokiteśvara!
His entire body descends into the wild grasses. "Great assembly, before Chengtian had appeared in the world, perhaps there was one or two patch-robed monks who harbored doubts.
Who would have known that after he appeared in the world, he reached a state where there were no words to be spoken and no principles to be grasped?"
Xin. Nevertheless, even so, we still rely on the presence of Master Houxu. Why is this? For ten thousand ages, no one has known it;
with the pupils in their eyes, they look upon the horse and rider.
Upon arriving, Guizong ascended the hall and said: "The true nature is the treasury of the mind-ground; it has neither head nor tail.
Responding to conditions to transform beings, it is expediently called 'wisdom. Great assembly, when Chengtian came here, he paid homage to Master Guizong, his uncle.
If the Master Uncle walked one zhang, Chengtian also walked one zhang; if the Master Uncle walked one chi, Chengtian likewise [walked one chi]."
To travel even one foot—what does this mean? To attain the place of wind and flow, one must simply manifest that wind and flow.

There are some fellows who, upon reaching this point, say, "The Yaśaṣka Stūpa is high; the Golden Wheel Peak is steep. But by the time they blink their eyes and turn their heads, the hawk has already flown beyond Silla.
Is it like this? Does it still accord with the tradition of my late master? Have you not heard it said: "To grind flour, one must use the local wheat;
to sing a song, one must be a man of the imperial capital"? Although this is so, thirty years hence, there will be a time of peace and tranquility as one crosses the waters.
Upon arriving at Kaixian, he ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'Do not travel the old path; do not don the original robe.
Now, if there are those who cast their bodies across the edge of a blade or reach out their hands within a flame, they are all merely laboring without merit."
How could one possibly carry water back to the riverhead to sell it? Nevertheless, even if a lady were to gaze into a bright mirror, one might say:
"There is no need for the application of rouge."
Upon arriving at Wanshan, he ascended the hall and said: "Yangshan said, 'If Master Shishu of Dongsi were still here, Huiji would not have reached such desolation.
On this day at Chengtian, I have come to see Master Shishu Wanshan; in this, one stroke has surpassed Yangshan. Why is this so? A single hand cannot clap alone;
both hands together produce a clear, resonant sound. Even though it is thus, tell me: does it still [fall short]?"
The Village Song Master asks: "How do you sing it? Is it 'Pointing the eyes to know another's intent;
see when the command is carried out'? Or is it 'Luo-lo li-luo-lo-li'? If it were like that, from antiquity to the present, they would be as numerous as hemp and millet.
Do you wish to understand? Once the mandarin ducks are embroidered, let the guest look at them; do not pass the golden needle to others."
Upon arriving at Qixian, he ascended the hall and said: "Since Chengtian first opened the hall, I have been arranging some entanglements, wandering aimlessly from south to north and east to west.
However, having stayed at Guizong, Kaishan, and Wanshan, I have now cleared them all away at once.
Today, arriving here at Sanxia, it is much like trying to treat a goiter on the eve of a wedding; one is suddenly at a loss for what to do."
I hope the assembly will not take offense. I humbly entreat you to take care of yourselves.
Upon arriving at the hall of the Arhat, he said: "In the past, the Patriarch Yin of this mountain possessed tongs capable of shattering empty space."
The spirit that scatters the white clouds was not without its utility at that time.
If one were to sit upon the hall today and bring about great peace, even a master hand would still be held back. Why then did Chengtian act with such haste today?
I do not see the Way as something to boast of one’s own purity to others; for the most part, it is essential that the distinction between the monastic and the lay be clear.
Returning to the Hall from the south of the mountain, he said: "Since I arrived here, how could there ever have been any interval?

For several days at Chengtian Temple, I walked around Mount Lu performing prostrations; every day, in my turning, stepping, bowing, and rising, I have not deceived you people by even a single point. You all—
While moving about, bowing, and turning within the courtyard, one cannot even casually receive a single point from Chengtian.
Why is it that Chengtian sees yet does not see? Do you wish to understand? Wherever there is a place, there are fragrant herbs; on what mountain is there no white cloud?
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "The former sages said, 'Every step one takes is the site of enlightenment. If a student were to go about in this manner, what would happen?
The Master said, "It makes people feel doubtful. The monk said, "I do not yet understand; I beg the Master to point it out again.
The Master said, "Even I cannot fully comprehend it. The monk bowed. The Master said, "What is there to understand? He then continued, "If you follow conditions..."
It is like the wind: blowing sand and rolling stones, yet not deviating from space. Simply, amidst phenomena, there is the penetration of non-phenomena.
Raising his staff, he said: "Seeing forms and hearing sounds—do not be deaf! He then struck the ground once with the staff and let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The former master said: 'Yangqi has no core meaning; he tills the fields to earn his meal.
Old Gautama is but a dreamer—where can one find his traces? Great assembly, who knows this? Under my current tenure at Chengtian, I reside in a small courtyard within the city.
Thus, I must trouble others to till the fields while I myself only know how to eat. Is this not so?
This means that if one raises a son who does not equal his father, the family will be poor for a generation. Nevertheless, it is said: "A great tree is wrapped in large bark;
a small tree is bound with small bark."

Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The old year has passed and the new year arrives again; what is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? The Master said: "The eyebrows are above the eyes. The monk said:
"If so, then the One Breath remains silent yet contains all forms; where do the myriad spirits go to thank the Impartial One?
The Master said: "I dare not grant you that. The monk said: "The assembly bears witness; I, this student, prostrate in thanks. The Master [nodded].
He said, "You must examine this more closely. He then said, "Today, throughout the world under heaven, everyone has added one year to their age.
Now tell me: has Nanquan’s water buffalo also added one year? Setting aside for a moment whether it has added or not, tell me: how much does the water buffalo’s nostril weigh?
If you can know its weight and distinguish its lightness and heaviness clearly, then every day you may deal with it as you please."
If others' crops and seedlings are not yet [ripe], on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, do not say that the grass turns green of its own accord when spring comes.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the expanse of the universe, there is a treasure hidden within the mountain of form.
Great assembly, the eyes are above the nose and the feet are below the belly; tell me, where does this treasure reside? He then said: "The human face..."
Knowing not where it has gone, the peach blossoms still smile at the spring breeze.
Entering the hall, he said: "When Mañjuśrī gave rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma, he was banished by the World-Honored One to the Iron Ring Mountains.
O Great Assembly! At that time, the World-Honored One acted as if he were contending over a minor matter and losing the major one; he lost the bearing of a Great Man. As for this...
Now, if there were someone here at Chengtian who gave rise to views of Buddha or views of Dharma, I, Chengtian, would never instruct them to stir or disturb those views.
Why is this so? Simply because once the snow has melted away, spring will naturally arrive.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the past, the Great Being Vimalakīrti, within his quarters in the city of Vaiśālī, manifested illness for the sake of all sentient beings who were ill.
O assembly, look at this ancient one acting thus; it is like tripping and falling on level ground.
Since the midsummer retreat, I, Chengtian, have suffered from dysentery for one month and have been convalescing for two months. Still...
Unable to find relief, how could there be any leisure? Regarding the illness of others, why do you act thus?
One who knows the timing and distinguishes what is appropriate is fit to be an *ācārya*.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said: 'When the superior man hears the Way, he practices it with diligence. When the man of middle capacity hears the Way, he is as if it exists and as if it is lost.
When the man of inferior capacity hears the Way, he laughs at it loudly. O Great Assembly!
If we speak from the standpoint of the patch-robed monks, we actually grant that those who laugh have some measure of backbone. Why is this so? Because the eyes of the multitude cannot be deceived."
Ascending the hall, he said: "All conditioned phenomena are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. Then, striking the meditation seat once, he said:
"How many times have black winds blown across the great ocean? Yet never have we heard of a fishing boat capsizing."

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "At the place where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking. What is it like when one speaks? The Master said, "Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun.
The monk said, "In that case, there is no place to set foot. The Master said, "Pounded by the pestle and ground by the millstone.
The monk said, "The official permits no needle, yet private passage allows for carts and horses. The Master said, "Worthwhile and worthless. The monk snapped his fingers once.
The Master said, "Precisely so. The monk stuck out his tongue. The Master said, "Poverty at home is still tolerable; poverty on the road is what kills one with grief.
The monk laughed heartily. The Master said, "Let it go. Then he said: "Where wisdom does not reach, you must by all means refrain from speaking."
"Great assembly, since this is a place where wisdom does not reach, what can even be said? [The Master] strikes the meditation seat once and says:
'When meeting, one may speak but three parts; one must not yet cast forth the whole heart.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Human sentiment is thick and heavy, while the Way-sentiment is subtle. The Way employs human sentiment; how could the world know this? Let me ask you all:
as you go about your daily affairs, is this human sentiment or the employment of the Way? Even if you could speak of it, it would still be human sentiment, not the employment of the Way.
This is truly like washing clods of earth in the mud. Do you wish to understand it clearly? Liang.
Jiuyun said: "A crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for a mere field mouse.
In the Dharma Hall, as the Master ascended the hall, a monk asked: "The hall of Shishuang is called 'the withered tree'; the seat at Deer Park is named 'the diamond.
On this day, what is the name of this new hall and seat at Chengtian? The Master replied: "Have you even left the household life yet? The monk remained silent.
The monk asked, "How can one ultimately describe 'being far removed'? The Master said, "There is a pillar right before you.
The monk bowed, and the Master then said, "The ancients said: 'This seat is so high and vast that I cannot ascend it; first, I must pay homage to Mount Sumeru and King Dīpa.'"
"Only then can one ascend. The great assembly, tell me: as for this seat at Chengtian, has it been ascending here for a long time, or does it only begin to ascend today?
If it only begins to ascend today, where has it been for all this time?
If it has been ascending for a long time, where is Mount Sumeru and King Lamp-Flower right now? He then picks up his staff and says: "Sumeru..."
Lamp-King, it is witnessed upon the tip of the staff. Each and every person possesses their own portion of this seat.
If you can see it thus, you may go to the city of Dongjing to hold the alms bowl, eat your meals in the city of Jiangzhou, enter the brothels, and pass through the wine shops;

you may watch as goods are bought cheaply at the southern end and sold dear at the northern end—never for a moment, not even a hair’s breadth, have you departed from this seat. And yet, although this is so...
Thus it was. Today, while the brilliant sun shone from the heavens and thunder and lightning crashed, Chengtian struck his meditation seat once with his staff and ascended the hall, saying:
"When the eye meets its object, one does not understand the Way; there is resonance within the words. When the feet move, how can one know the path? Color emerges from the lacquer box."
"Household! This is why I have said to you, gentlemen: who would dare to err with you by even a single hair’s breadth? Do you understand?
The transgressions of Chengtian are already no small matter."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "Leaping upon the edge of a blade. Then, laying the staff across his lap, he said, "Riding a horse within a mote of dust;
toiling away, going and coming—this is the one who is truly awake. He then cast down the staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To withdraw the profound mechanism before its signs appear; to conceal the dark operation within the very process of transformation. O Great Assembly!
Now, every single one of you Chan practitioners comes forward with a bearing like that of a king; when questioned, your eloquence flows like a cascading river. What can be done about that?
But what if you could suddenly press down the clouds and listen as Chengtian speaks some words of 'treating the existent as non-existent'? He then went on.
Only by going forth does one come to know. Beating the drum and playing the lute, one must encounter those who understand both assemblies.
Although this is so, where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The one moon universally appears in all waters; the moons in all waters are subsumed within the one moon. Raising his staff, he said:

"In Pūrvavideha to the east, Aparagoyānī to the west, Jambudvīpa to the south, and Uttarakuru to the north—even in Silla and Bohai—those among the assembly today who are even slightly engaged in study all know that [the moon] is upon the tip of this staff. And...
When it comes to asking about the length of another’s ladle handle or the size of their cooking pot, one can be certain that nineteen out of twenty will not know.
Thus it is said: "Only at nightfall does one see the person holding the needle. If you have not yet reached this state, then: "The bright moon fills the boat, a single bamboo pole;
my home is on the Five Lakes—come, let us return! He struck his staff once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "There has never been delusion; do not seek enlightenment. Why, then, from the beginning until now, have there been lineages of teachers and patriarchs?
If you understand this, you will follow local customs upon entering a village. If you do not understand, you will starve to death on Mount Shouyang.
Nevertheless, even so, when entering the water, one sees the tall man."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "If you can understand it here, it is like adding frost to snow.
If you have not yet reached this point, simply wait for the snow to melt; then, naturally, spring will arrive. He struck the ground once with the staff.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said: 'Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha, run past with haste.
Therefore, at times Chengtian’s mouth was like a wooden stump; at times his words were like splitting bamboo; at times he praised or censured the people of the world;
and at times he left it entirely to the people of the world to praise or censure him. Even so, O Great Assembly, three thousand miles away..."
"One must not err when meeting people.
He ascended the hall and said: "To study the Way within this [teaching] is like the earth supporting a mountain, unaware of the mountain's towering loftiness;
it is like a stone containing jade, unaware of the jade's flawlessness. If one can act in this manner, that is true renunciation. O Great Assembly, since this is so..."
One knows the mountain’s solitary loftiness, yet one does not know that the jade is without flaw. But tell me, who is it that speaks thus?
He then strikes the meditation seat once and says: "If the root of the tooth does not pass through the water, one cannot avoid conforming to human sentiment."
Ascending the hall, he raised the verse by Yunmen: "A phrase that does not reveal its wind-bone, Delivered before a word is even spoken.
As you step forward with your mouth chattering, I know you are utterly deluded. "Great assembly, this old man Yunmen only knew how to claim supremacy where there is no Buddha."
Furthermore, he does not understand how to transform customs or change social mores. Cheng Tian has fashioned one for himself and presents it to the assembly:

a phrase that reveals no underlying structure, yet possesses both salt and vinegar. Rely on you gentlemen to examine it closely; a nine-bend pearl is difficult to string. Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Great Elephant does not travel upon the rabbit’s path; great enlightenment is not constrained by petty details. What words are these?
To follow the Way, one must leap forth as a fierce dragon from within the eye of a needle, and unfold the world within a single strand of lotus fiber. Why is this so?
When merit is abundant and karma is matured, the channel is completed once the water arrives. *Chán* (Investigate!)"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Light does not illuminate the object; the object, likewise, does not exist. Raising his staff, he said:

"This staff—when it encounters the noble, it is base; when it encounters the base, it is noble. Why is this so? Who knows that within cold ashes, the fragrance of nine-fold refinement permeates the bottle?
He struck the ground with the staff and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the winter solstice; on this day, the first yang arises. He then picked up his staff and said, "Tell me, assembly, what is this?
If you can grasp it just as it is, then you will accordingly receive blessings in accordance with the season."
If we calculate until the New Year’s court, there will still be much snow ahead.
This is why Chengtian usually speaks ten times and stops nine. Why is this so? One should not plant thorny brambles at the gate;
later generations’ descendants will get caught by them. Even so, thirty years from now, Grandfather Lü will fish. *Chān*.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you can understand where the black bean has not yet sprouted, you will see that from antiquity to the present, the few cannot withstand the many.

If one says, 'The arm is long, so the sleeves of the robe are short; the leg is thin, so the straw sandals are wide,' let the people of the world at large laugh as they please, saying that Chengtian is not clever enough.
Nevertheless, whether there is profit or loss, one does not leave the marketplace."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If it were always like today, Chengtian would be deceiving you, all you venerable seniors.
If it were not like today, Chengtian could not deceive you, all you venerable seniors. Why is this so? Because one sides with principle, not with kinship. *Can* (I take my leave)."

Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered and settled, he said, "Does the great assembly understand? He struck the floor once with his staff and said, "Two rows of tears upon the coral pillow;
half are for thinking of you, half are for resenting you. He then descended from his seat.
Recorded by the junior disciple Haitan, this is the *Yulu* (Discourse Record) of Chan Master Chongsheng of Yuantong Monastery in Jiangzhou.
On the day the Master accepted his invitation, he ascended the seat and looked over the assembly, saying: "In the past, Sansheng said: 'Whenever I encounter a person...'"
"Come out! Come out! If you come out, you are no longer a person. When Xinghua heard this, he said, "I am not like that.
When I meet a person, I do not come out; when I come out, I am already a person. "Great assembly, each of these two venerable masters has a point where they hit the mark.
But tell me, which one was first and which one was last? Is there anyone here who can settle this for certain?"—Liang.
Jiuyun said: "Do not boast of hands that whirl like snow in a wondrous dance; the three stages must all be urged forward by everyone together.

He descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said: "Entering the forest without stirring the grass; entering the water without disturbing the waves; entering among birds without confusing their flight. Great Assembly!"
This is the very hand and foot used for hauling in the anchor and setting sail. But tell me, how should a monk of the patched-robes school act?
[He] struck the meditation seat once with his hand and said: "Turning over mountains and seas to seek a true friend; stirring up heaven and earth to see Great Peace."
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "When a single bubble arises, the waves begin. He struck it again and said:
"When a single bubble arises, Mañjuśrī appears. Then he struck it three times in succession and asked: "And as for this—what then? After a long silence, he said:
"Who knows that in the distant mist and billows, there is yet another way of thinking? "Investigate!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'To offer this profound mind to every dust mote and land is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.
Yuan Tong does not think so. At times one boils wild vegetables with their roots; at times one gathers mountain firewood with its leaves and burns it. *Chan*."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddha-body is unconditioned; it does not fall within the realm of numerical categories.

Now tell me, from where do the six sense bases, the twelve links of dependent origination, the eighteen elements, and even the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates come? Striking the meditation seat once with his hand, he said:
'A fine woman does not wear her wedding dress. *Chan*."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The clay Buddha does not cross water; the wooden Buddha does not cross fire; the golden Buddha does not cross the furnace. Great assembly!
Old Man Zhaozhou’s twelve joints of bone and eighty-four thousand pores have all been cast into your laps at once.
Today, Yuantong, seeing injustice on the road, shall vent his indignation on behalf of the ancients. (He struck with his hand.)

He struck the meditation seat once and said: "One must know that the seas and mountains submit to the enlightened sovereign; one has not yet believed that heaven and earth can trap a person of auspicious virtue.
*Chan.* Entering the hall, he said: "Originally there is no wound; do not injure it. Nevertheless, even so, without a single event..."
"One long wisdom. [Pause.
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff, held it horizontally across his knees, and said: "Spring grows and summer matures. Setting the staff down, he said:
"Rain follows its course and wind is harmonious. He descended from the seat.

On the day he received the purple robe, he ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'If the ox leading the plow goes toward the east of the water, one cannot avoid the royal corvée labor of the government.
If the ox leading the plow goes toward the west of the water, one cannot avoid the royal corvée labor of the government.
It is better to simply accept whatever little is allotted. Now, tell me, assembly: what is this 'little'? Thereupon, he picked up his *kāṣāya*.
Sajiao said: "Is this not a bit of something? Nevertheless, even so:
'If one sees me by form, or seeks me by sound, such a person walks a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata. Then he let it drop and said:
'May we rejoice that all under heaven is at peace. *Chan*."
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Yunmen’s handling of Sanping’s verse, which says: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing;
there is no further sound or form to present to you. What sounds or forms are there for the mouth? If one understands this point, there is nothing remaining;

essence and function do not hinder one another, whether they are divided or not. He then took up his staff and said, "The staff is the essence," and then pointed to the lantern and said, "The lantern..."
The basket is for use. How can one not distinguish it? Great assembly, Yunmen only knows how to paint the eyebrows according to the model.
Yuan Tong is not so: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; there are no further sounds or forms to present to you. The eye is the eye, the ear is the ear.
If one understands this, there is nothing else remaining. As for essence and function, whether they are distinguished or not makes no difference. (45)
"A hundred lanes of flowers and willows; two or three thousand pavilions of pipes and strings.
*Paṇ*. He ascends the hall. He cites a monk asking Touzi: "When one enters nirvana without severing afflictions, what then?
Touzi made a grimace and said, "This monk is fond of stirring up karma to kill people. Xitang offered a different response: "Every household contemplates the world."
Yin. The assembly! Touzi may be said to have been skilled at assessing talent; Xitang may be said to have been skilled at filling offices.
Suppose someone were to ask Yuan Tong today: "How is it when one enters nirvana without severing the afflictions? One would immediately say to him:
"Green mountains and blue waters; a short oar on a solitary boat."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Attendant Wang, who went to Linji and asked, "Do the monks in the hall read sutras every day?
Linji said, "They do not read sutras. He asked again, "Do they practice meditation? Linji said, "They do not practice meditation. [Wang] asked, "What exactly do they do?
Linji said, "I teach them all to become Buddhas and Patriarchs. Attendant Wang said, "Though gold dust is precious, if it falls..."
"The eye has become clouded. Furthermore, how is it? Linji said, "I took you for a common man.
"Great assembly, Linji truly possesses only one eye. If it were Perfect Penetration, it would not be so. Although gold dust is precious,"
"It falls into the eye and becomes a cataract. Again, how is it so? "I took you for a common worldly man. "The assembly, try to decide this! He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case: A monk asked Dongshan, "When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them? Dongshan said, "Why do you not..."
"Go to the place where there is neither cold nor heat. A monk asked, "What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat?
Dongshan said, "When it is cold, I freeze you to death; when it is hot, I scorch you to death. Dongshan possesses all flavors. Later on, how should one respond?
If someone were to suddenly ask Yuancong, "What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat? he would strike them across the spine with his staff. Study this!
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you have not yet found a point of entry, you must find a point of entry.
Once you have found a point of entry, you must not辜负 (fail to honor) this old monk. Great assembly, the old man of Muzhou may be said to have experienced much;
when he wishes to sit, he sits; when he wishes to walk, he walks. Nevertheless, even so, Heaven does not possess complete mastery."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said: "Step back three paces.
"What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'? The Master said: "When power is in one's hand for a day, observe when the command is carried out.

"What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said: "The head of the staff has broken off. "What is 'neither taking away the person nor taking away the environment'? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
The Master said, "Every household contemplates Avalokiteśvara.
A monk asked, "Why did the hundred birds bring flowers to offer when Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "Worldly sentiments perceive cold and warmth. The monk asked, "After he had seen him, why did the hundred birds no longer bring flowers to offer? The Master said, "People..."
His expression shifted according to the rise and fall of the situation, and he said: "If one atom is established, the state and its people will flourish, yet the village elders will frown.

If not even one atom is established, the state and its people will perish, yet the village elders will be at peace. "Great assembly, tell me: is it right to establish it, or is it right not to establish it?
After a long silence, he said: "The heart does not betray others; the face shows no shame. He struck the meditation seat once with his hand.
[The Master] says: "Enter. He descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he says: "The mind turns with the myriad objects; where it turns, it is truly profound. O Great Assembly!
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are performing somersaults upon the eyebrows of each of you. If you do not see this, you will be deceived by them. If you do see it—"
"You may go. He then bowed and awaited instructions. [The Master] suddenly picked up his staff, called to the assembly, and said, "Each of you return to the hall.
He then cast down the staff, descended from the seat, and departed.
He ascended the hall. After a long silence, he looked back at the assembly and said, "As for this very thing, how many can leap out of it?
If you cannot leap out, I do not say that you do not know; yet alas, your body follows its shadow.
If you can leap out, you would have known long ago that the lamp is fire, and the rice would have been cooked long before now. He then descended from his seat. *Chan*.
Ascending the hall, he said: "How extraordinary! How truly extraordinary! The insentient preach the Dharma—how inconceivable! If you listen with your ears, you will never understand;
only when hearing sound through the faculty of sight can you know it. He raised his whisk and asked, "Do you hear it? If you say you hear it, I deafen your ears.
If you say you do not hear it, I blind your eyes. Tell me, what is it then? He struck [the floor] with the whisk.
[He brandishes] the whisk. Striking the meditation seat once, he says: "The great trichiliocosm is but a bubble in the ocean; all sages and worthies are like a flash of lightning.
Entering the hall, he says: "Life and death alternate; cold and heat shift in turn. That things flow and change is the common condition of humanity."—Sengzhao.
The Dharma Master said, "I truly do not know what it is that does not move along with things. What is this 'not moving'?
After a long silence, he said, "A large month has thirty days; a small month has twenty-nine."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Leaves fall and return to the root; when one comes, there are no words.
"Great assembly, the Patriarch may truly be said to be skilled at 'borrowing a hand to perform a fist. There are some fellows who often say, 'The words are still ringing in our ears.
Have you not heard it said: 'Ziqi has gone and does not return; how lamentable this vast expanse! One knows not who else within heaven and earth is a true connoisseur. Study this!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "A bird has two wings; its flight knows no distance. The Way issues from a single corner; its practice knows no before or after.
You monks, in your daily lives, setting down the spoon and picking up the chopsticks, all claim to 'know it. Yet when you reach the summit of the ridge, why is it that you suddenly run out of breath?
Have you not heard it said: 'If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate anxieties'?"
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “In the cauldron of boiling water, there is no place that is cold.
The monk asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, “Pressing down a gourd underwater. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, “The crow flies and the hare runs. Then he said: “The river moon shines; the pine wind blows. At this point, is there anyone who has not passed through the net?”
[He said: "What about this? After a long silence, he said: "The August Heaven has no partiality.

At that time, the Master was in the West Hall of the Fifth Patriarch when he accepted an invitation. Ascending the seat, he said: "In the preface just now, it was stated:
'Quiescent illumination without movement is concentration; responding and thereby penetrating all things is wisdom. [The Master] picked up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:
'Is this concentration? Is this wisdom? Is there anyone who can discern it? Since there is none, I cannot help but proceed according to the original sequence, starting from the first chapter."
By means of the Way, one plays at unfolding and rolling up; this is the domain of the patch-robed monk. It is a matter of winning the periphery:
when one wishes to unfold, the Buddhas of the three periods are upon the tip of the staff; when one wishes to roll up, they are entrusted to Deshan and Linji.
Tell me, today: is it rolling up or unfolding? After a long silence, he said: "Limitless tree-tops, the wind passes by their ears. Furthermore, the Cowherd Boy—
"Ong yi! [With this, he struck the meditation seat once with his staff.

That night, the assembly requested a small discourse (*saṃkṣepa-kathā*). A monk asked: "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it arises only by relying on conditions. Now that the patron has come in person to welcome you..."
"Please, Master, preach the Dharma. The Master said, "Nine times nine is eighty-one. The monk said, "I, this student, do not yet understand the essential meaning within this.
I pray that the Master will use skillful means to proclaim it again. The Master said, "Go ask the pillar. The monk said, "Is this not precisely where the Master benefits people?
The Master said, "It would put all bystanders to laughter. The monk bowed. He asked, "Seeking nothing from the various sages, and not esteeming oneself..."

"Numen (ling). This is not yet the matter within the scope of a patch-robed monk (naseng). What is the matter within the scope of a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "Dead water does not harbor dragons.
The monk asked, "If one goes forth in this very manner, what then? The Master said, "You will be utterly deceived.
The monk said, "The streams and mountains differ, but the clouds and moon are the same. The Master said, "This is even further removed from the point. The monk said, "To deceive me alone!"
[The monk] said, "I have attained it immediately. The Master said, "But what about the eyes of the great assembly? The Master continued, "You have become a mediocre patch-robed monk.
The monk said, "Let me pass one move. The Master struck the meditation seat once. The monk then bowed. The Master then said:

"The Buddha-body fills the Dharma-realm, universally manifesting before all living beings. Responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not reach; yet it always remains [in its original state]."
Regarding this seat of enlightenment, O Great Assembly: how can one explain the principle of responding to conditions and manifesting according to needs?

It is simply that, within the space of a single snap of the fingers, the capacities and karmic conditions of all sentient beings throughout the entire world-system are met with complete sufficiency, yet not so much as a single hair’s breadth is moved.
This is what is called "responding to conditions and manifesting according to needs," while remaining eternally upon this very seat. Just so...
I, this mountain monk, have here accepted an invitation for the *Lotus Sūtra*. I am about to take my leave of the assembly and depart.
Once I have finished opening the hall at Susong County, I shall return to the monastery. Now tell me: have I left this seat or not?
If you say I have left, that is merely the circulation of worldly conventions (*saṃvṛti*). If you say I have not left, how do you perceive that matter of non-leaving? Is it not simply "no"?
The realms of the peripheral lands are not separated from one another by so much as a hair’s tip;
the ten ages of past and present do not depart from the single moment of the present thought. Furthermore, is it that all things are mindless and spontaneously pervade everything at once?

If you think so, you are merely striking the moon with a falling staff. At this point, you must attain awakening before you can succeed. You say: "Once awakened, one simply rests. But what else is there to do?

One must inevitably encounter another person. At the moment when the "hanging hand" expedient is employed, there is naturally a path for emergence at every step, so as not to blind the eyes of the student.

If one only attains the realization of a "dry radish," not only will you blind the eyes of the student, but furthermore, as soon as you move, you will first strike the point of the blade and wound your own hand. Look at me, Yangqi—first...
The Master asked of the venerable teacher Ciming: "When the dark birds warble their cries and leave the clouds to enter the jumbled peaks—how is this?

He replied: "I walk amidst the wild weeds; you, again, have entered a deep village. [The student] pressed further: "An official does not allow even a needle to pass; may I ask one more question? The venerable teacher then gave a shout.
[The student] said: "A fine shout! The venerable teacher shouted again. My late teacher also shouted. The venerable teacher [then said]: "..."
He then gave two consecutive shouts. The former master thereupon prostrated and withdrew. The assembly must understand this:

those who have attained realization and encounter others meet at the crossroads of the street, yet they clasp hands atop a thousand peaks; they meet atop a thousand peaks, yet they clasp hands at the crossroads of the street.

Therefore, I, this mountain monk, have often composed a verse on this: Meeting people at the crossroads, Yet clasping hands atop a thousand peaks; Meeting atop a thousand peaks, Yet clasping hands at the crossroads.
Where others dwell, I do not dwell; where others walk, I do not walk.
I have untied the mouth of the sack and scattered its contents all at once before everyone. Those with eyes, do not mistake this for something else.

On the day of his departure from the Fifth Patriarch’s monastery, the Master ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the strategic maneuvers within the tent;

what will be the situation as you set out on this journey today? The Master replied, "One sees the road while riding the horse. The monk said, "If that is so, then the gift of gold will once again be relied upon."
The rain of flowers falls separately upon each direction. The Master said, "The one who went ahead has not yet arrived; the end becomes the beginning.

The monk said, "When the road is long, one knows the strength of the horse; when years have passed, one discerns the character of the person. The Master said, "Thank you for seeing me off. He then said:
"In the Liang Dynasty, Master Zhigong sent someone to deliver a message to Chan Master Dazhi of Mount Nanyue: 'Why do you not descend the mountain to save and deliver sentient beings?'"
"What is the point of gazing at the Milky Way? Daoshi turned back and delivered this message: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have all been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where else could there be any sentient beings left to deliver? "Great assembly, the old man Daoshi is like one who hammers a stake while rowing a boat;
he knows only the first part, but not the second. I, this mountain monk, am not so. I reside at Chengtian."

When he finished his affairs in the city, he stayed at Yuantong; when he finished his affairs at the head of the road, he came to the Fifth Patriarch’s place and sat upon the high seat in the West Hall.
Now, as he departs for Fahua, he strikes the gavel from his seat, saying:
"Who can manage the idle affairs of the Buddhas of the three periods? Why is this so? 'Meeting on the road, one does not dismount; each has their own journey ahead.'"

On the day of opening the hall, after the incense has been offered and the prayers for the Emperor have been concluded, he says: "The transmission of the School is raised in a single stroke, yet it has already fallen into the second or third [generation].
The ancient road is level and plain, yet travelers remain oblivious to it themselves. Only those who shift their bodies and change their steps know it;
is there anyone here today who has reached it? Come forth and see! A monk asks: "The Bhagavans of the ten directions all enter through the one path to Nirvana. [He] raises his hand...
He made a single stroke and said, "The ancients who reached this point had not yet attained the ultimate. How do you act for the sake of others, Monk?
The teacher said, "You have already missed it. The monk said, "Today I have personally seen Fahua. The teacher said, "The one phrase beneath your heels."
"How do you say it? A monk said, "I have another way of thinking about it. The Master said, "I told you already—you missed it. The monk bowed.
A monk asked, "One shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function operate simultaneously. Apart from these two paths, please, Master, speak otherwise.
The Master then shouted. The monk said, "I have always doubted you, Master. The Master struck him. The monk said, "An adept! The Master— [struck him again].
"It is not enough," he said. The monk bowed, and the Master then said: "In the past, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the World-Honored One held up a flower, and Kāśyapa smiled.
The World-Honored One said, 'I entrust this Treasury of the True Dharma Eye to Mahākāśyapa;
let it be transmitted in succession so that it never be severed. It has come down to this day, O Great Assembly. If it is indeed the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye..."
As for the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the Old Man Śākyamuni himself had no share in it; with what could he have entrusted it? With what could he have transmitted it? Why is this so?
Furthermore, within the sphere of each and every person, there is already a Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of one’s own. Every day when you rise, [you possess it].
Right and wrong, north and south—every variety of action and manifestation is entirely the light and shadow of the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye.

When this eye opens, heaven and earth, the great world, the sun, moon, and stars, and the myriad phenomena of the forested universe are all right before one’s face, yet not even a hair’s breadth of form is seen.
When this eye has not yet opened, they are all entirely within the eyes of every person.

Those who have already opened [this eye] today are not subject to this limit. As for those who have not yet opened it, this mountain monk, without sparing his hand, shall open this Treasury of the Dharma Eye for you all to behold.
He then raised his hand, held up two fingers, and said: "Look! Look! If you can see it, then..."
The matter is as one family. If this is still not clear, this mountain monk cannot help but speak another verse:
"The Dharma-eye treasury of all people—none of the thousand sages can equal it. For your sake, I open a single thread; its radiance fills the Great Tang. Sumeru enters the sea;
in the sixth month, bitter frost descends. Though the Lotus Sūtra speaks thus, there is no phrase to be deliberated upon. Assembly, since it is full...
The oral explanation is finished. Why, then, is there no phrase by which one may deliberate? He then gave a shout and said, "Look at the body divided into two places.
On the day of entering the monastery, he ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Having departed far from the ancestral peaks and already arrived at the Lotus [Sūtra], what is immovability?"
The Master said, "The entire assembly sees it. The monk asked, "I do not yet understand; what is the matter within it? The Master said, "Look up.
The monk said, "In that case, the Prince’s Peak is high and the moon over the Songjiang is bright.
The Master said, "Only then is it so. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "An ancient said, 'Speaking is not as good as practicing. Today, with you..."
"Great assembly, both the teaching has reached its end and the practice has reached its end. For now, we may rejoice that the world is at peace. But tell me:
how would you express the phrase 'standing firmly on solid ground'? After a long silence, he said: "In the end, water must flow toward the sea;
in the final analysis, clouds must seek the mountains to return."
The next day, he ascended the hall and said: "An ancient said: 'Having chosen a secluded dwelling to suit my rustic sentiments, throughout the year there is neither parting nor welcoming.
Sometimes I ascend straight to the peak of a solitary mountain; beneath the moon, I strip away the clouds and let out a single cry.
Tonight, this mountain monk arrived here, yet I have had no leisure to ascend the peak of the solitary mountain. Furthermore, it is a dark night with no moon; I remain only within the Dharma Hall."
"Inside the hall. He lets out several long whistles. "Do you all hear them? If you say you do not hear them, you may be said to be deceiving yourself.
But if you do hear them, with what do you hear? He strikes the meditation staff once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When I press my finger, the Sea-Seal radiates light. Holding up his staff, he said:

"Mountains, rivers, the great earth, waterfowl, and forest trees—all sentient and insentient beings today, upon the tip of this *Dharmapada* staff, let out the great lion’s roar and expound the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*. Now tell me, what do Tiantai and Nanyue say?"
Regarding the Dharma-gate: Nanyue spoke of the Five Ranks of Dongshan’s practice—sovereign and minister, father and son—each attaining its proper place.
"Do not cling to the green grass in a cold cave; sitting amidst white clouds, the school is not subtle.

Tiantai spoke of Linji’s Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, the Four Selections, and how a single shout distinguishes guest and host, with illumination and function operating simultaneously. To understand this, one must grasp the essence within.
"Intention! At noon, they strike the third watch. Lushan comes forth and says: 'You two are right in the midst of a tangle of vines.
Have you not heard it said: 'If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata.
O Assembly, if these three men's views are weighed on the scale of a true monk, one weighs eight *liang*, and one..."
"Weighing half a catty, yet one of them is not worth even half a penny. Now tell me, which one is not worth half a penny?
After a long silence, he said, "I only wish that the spring breeze would exert its full strength and blow all at once into my gate. He struck the ground once with his staff.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said: 'Throughout the entire earth, there is not a single person who can truly proclaim the religious teaching.

Even if there were one person who could proclaim the religious teaching, throughout the entire earth, all would have their blades blunted and their tongues tied, losing their very bodies and lives—yet this is merely a holeless iron hammer.
Great assembly, the ancients had salt in their vinegar; you must have eyes upon your tongues."
Only then can one begin to discern it. If you can indeed discern it, only then will you know that the unperforated iron hammer cannot be penetrated by the wind nor moistened by the rain.
Today at the Lotus Assembly, I shall once again recite a verse; then, raising his voice, he said: "The unperforated iron hammer goes on its rounds through the hall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To be able to graft an unrooted tree and to be able to light a lamp from the bottom of the sea—this is not yet the business of a patch-robed monk.
But tell me, what is the business of a patch-robed monk? After a long silence, he said: "Twice a day the almsbowl gets wet."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Elder Śākyamuni has four great vows: 'Vows to sever the boundless afflictions;
vows to study the boundless Dharma gates; vows to deliver the boundless sentient beings; and vows to realize unexcelled Bodhi.'"
The Lotus Sūtra also contains the four great vows: When hunger comes, one must eat; when cold arrives, one adds clothing;
when weary, one stretches out the legs to sleep; and in the heat, one desires a breeze.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The eighth day of the fourth month is the Buddha’s Birthday Festival. Those with eyebrows and eyes all pass down this tradition. 'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
One wonders how many have had their skull-caps split open! Skull-caps split open? Strike them once with a staff and give them to a dog to eat!"
Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Xuedou, who said: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure.
Vast and silent between heaven and earth, standing alone, what can one gaze upon to the limit? Then, turning back, he asked the attendant, "Is there anyone guarding the abbot’s quarters?"

He said, "Yes. He said himself, "The heart of a thief is always suspicious. "Great Assembly," [he continued], "the Elder Xuedou has the hand that can release and gather, expanding and contracting heaven and earth.
Nevertheless, even so, how does it compare to 'Heaven and Earth cannot contain it;
Yao and Shun do not know its name'? Today Fahua cannot restrain his impatience; he shall now speak out on behalf of the ancients, and thus said: "The Mountain..."
The cherry blossoms glow like flames; the mountain birds’ songs are smooth and melodious. Hand in hand, we do not share the same path; let the spring airs blossom as they will.
Since heaven and earth first came into being, how many have possessed living eyes? Today, the Lotus Sutra briefly emerges;
no longer need one ask the attendant to guard the abbot’s quarters.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The beginning of the summer retreat is named 'prohibiting the feet. The meaning of 'prohibiting the feet' lies in advancing on the Path and protecting living beings.
But for us monks, what further life is there to protect, and what Path is there to advance upon? *Spit! Spit!*"
Spitting upon the face of Old Śākyamuni, he takes a single step and tramples the vertebrae of Old Śākyamuni’s back.
Yet, such a person is still merely one who follows in the tracks and joins the ranks; they are not yet a monk of the true lineage. After a long silence, he said:
"How much boundless elegance is there to be peddled? It is better to let people avoid pointing at a fine gentleman."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Today at Fahua, I have caught a cold. For now, I shall speak of entanglements within the second level of responsiveness.
He raised his staff, struck it three times, and set it down.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Though one might spend ten thousand taels of gold daily, it is not valued at the Gate of the Lotus Sutra.

Even if something were not worth half a penny, one would have merely entered the Gate of the Lotus Sutra; yet one would not have ascended the Hall of the Lotus Sutra, nor entered the Chamber of the Lotus Sutra."
Now tell me, what kind of person can ascend the Hall of the Lotus Sutra and enter the Chamber of the Lotus Sutra? He then said: "His eyes have three corners;
his head towers over the Five Peaks."
Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while and then said, "I have already finished painting legs on a snake.
He descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he cited the teachings which state: "All sentient beings possess a mind; those who possess a mind shall all attain Buddhahood.
He then cited the Patriarch’s words: "Though all possess a mind, they are as far apart as heaven and earth. He asked, "In saying these things, is there not a contradiction?"
"What? How can one avoid contradiction? After a long silence, he said: "The Persian's nostrils are vermilion;
Lohita’s fist is as large as an almsbowl. When weary, he knocks down Mount Sumeru; with a roar, he slaughters Avalokiteśvara of Potalaka."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Gold-Luan Worthy. One day, while standing before the kitchen, he saw the head cook and asked him:
"Head Cook, you have certainly succeeded in transforming the raw into the cooked; now, setting aside the wooden ladle, bring me a single phrase. The head cook was speechless.

Later, the Master ordered the monks in his private quarters to provide a substitute response on his behalf, but none were in accord. He then provided the answer himself: "The mutton stew is a medley of flavors. The assembly [applauded].
"The mouth is difficult to regulate. The Great Assembly, tell me: has Jinluan been able to part from the wooden ladle yet? Fahuā is not like this;
having cast aside the wooden ladle, how do you speak this one phrase? "If human relations are good, even drinking water will nourish you."
Ascending the hall, he raised [this case]: "Xuansha often said, 'I place you all upon the crown of my head,' not daring to err with you by even a hair’s breadth.
When the ancients spoke thus, tell me: was he in error, or was he not?
If you say he was not in error, why did he place you upon the crown of his head? Therefore, Fahua usually [speaks] to all...
People merely meet as equals; even so, they still fear making a mistake. To speak in such a way is like committing an offense intentionally despite knowing better.
Nevertheless, before those with clear eyes, one must not err in one's presentation.
Ascending the hall, he said: "This year the rain has been exceptionally abundant; one can surely expect the harvests throughout the land to ripen this autumn.
Cowherds everywhere sing songs of peace, bringing a laugh to Old Wang of the eastern village."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Lotus Sūtra has gathered three kinds of rare and marvelous treasures. Have they ever been brought forth in ordinary times?
Today, as Ma-tou and Gu-tou set out on their journey, I cannot help but bring them forth to present to you two gentlemen. Thereupon, he raised his staff.
[The Master] strikes the desk three times and says: "First of all, you must not split it apart; furthermore, you must divide it between both hands.
Even if you encounter a ship’s captain from the Southern Barbarians, you must still exchange his very eyes."
On the Mid-Autumn Day, he ascended the hall and said: "The question lies within the answer; the answer lies within the question—let that be for now.
But tell me, where does it reside when there is neither question nor answer? After a long silence, he said: "This night, the single orb is full; where is its pure light not present?"
He Fei invited the Master, but he did not go. Upon returning to the mountain after withdrawing from his post in the prefecture, he ascended the hall and said:
"I did not dwell in the city walls, as I had intended; Mountain flowers and birds again frolic together. Last night, the stone spring passed before my window;
What is it that its clear sound surpasses that of old? He struck the floor three times with his staff.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Every phenomenon is the original Dharma; there is no phenomenon and no non-phenomenon.
Why, within a single phenomenon, would there be that which is a phenomenon and that which is not? O Great Assembly! Mountains, rivers, and the great earth; form and emptiness, light and darkness;
the myriad phenomena of the forested world—blue, yellow, red, and white—all possess distinct essences and names, clearly manifest. Monks are monks; laypeople are laypeople. How can one explain this?"
"One Dharma. Is it this shouting once, clapping once, or raising a single finger? If you act in such a way, you have not even seen it in a dream.
So, how can you say it? After a long silence, he said: "The morning sun melts the snow upon the cliffside;
the night tides pound the vines by the seashore."
On account of the snow, he ascended the hall and said: "Heaven and earth do not allow even the slightest deficiency; after winter, the snow falls according to the season.

The obstructing vapors of the old year have forever vanished, and extraordinary auspicious signs appear far and wide. The seasonal rites are perfectly suited to be thus. Do not let the Lord of Heaven leak his secrets away!
Why must you not let the Lord of Heaven leak his secrets? A gentleman bestows grace without looking for recompense."
On New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said: “Meeting one another, we greet each other with joy; at once, all are thoroughly scrutinized. The *fuhou* turban points its toes toward heaven.”
