Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, “Who is it that attains the essential meaning of Huangmei?
The Sixth Patriarch replied, “One who understands the Buddha-Dharma attains it. The monk asked, “Does the Master attain it? The Patriarch said, “I do not. The monk asked, “Why do you not?
The Patriarch said, “I do not understand the Buddha-Dharma. “Great assembly, do you recognize the Patriarch?”
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: When Chan Master Changsha returned from traveling the mountains, the Head Seat asked him, "Where have you been coming from, Preceptor?
Changsha said, "At first I followed the fragrant grasses away; now I follow the falling blossoms back. The Head Seat said, "This is very much like the spirit of spring.
Changsha said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping on lotuses. "Tell me, everyone: was Changsha in spring, summer, autumn, or winter?"
It is within, yet it does not reside within spring, summer, autumn, or winter. Do you understand? A single breath speaks not, yet it contains all forms;
where could the myriad spirits fail to express their gratitude for this impartiality?
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Master Dongshan, "When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them?
Dongshan said, "Why not go to a place where there is neither cold nor heat? The monk asked, "What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat? Dongshan said:
"In winter, cold kills the *śrāmaṇera*; in summer, heat kills the *śrāmaṇera*. Old Dongshan, you always try to bring spring to withered wood—how do you go about it?
Today Baiyun shall give you a hand; today is the opening of the furnace."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the example of Venerable Baizhang, who said: "You all shall cultivate the fields for me, and I shall expound the Great Meaning for you.
One day, when the assembly had finished cultivating the fields, they said: "The field cultivation is complete; we request the Master to expound the Great Meaning.
Baizhang spread out his two hands and walked several paces. "The assembly—Baizhang expounded the Great Meaning in this manner. Do you all remember it?"
Is it so? Today Baiyun speaks this matter once more for you all. I have always admired Baizhang’s ability to clear the fields;
it has been passed from hand to hand by practitioners of past and present. Who would say his tongue never moved? The five notes and six scales revolve with perfect harmony.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold within those very eyes.
If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, and speech. Raising his staff, he said: "This here is the staff;
which one is the true essence of the Great Way? With what do you attempt to perceive it? You lot, you team of lacquer buckets! [He struck them. "In the middle of the twelfth month..."
For thirty days, he recognized only the bridge of a donkey’s saddle as his father’s chin;
then he shouted, “Go! He ascended the hall and said: “Those who speak lose the truth; those who know fall back into ignorance;
those who possess it deviate from their nature; those who lack it harm their own person. If you understand this, it is like fanning the fire with the wind—no great effort is required. If...
Nor will it. "The autumn waters share one color with the vast sky. And yet, even so, there are times when riding upon the bright moon, one does not realize one has passed through Cangzhou.

Chan Master Yan, the Head Seat, accepted an invitation from the Four Directions and ascended the hall, saying: "Year after year, the autumn heat remains as intense as at the beginning. What matter is this purity?"
The coolness is truly abundant; it is entirely the resonance of the people's own minds. It was not in vain that [Master] Bo Jue held hands at Longshu.
But tell me, how would you say this phrase about "holding hands"? After a long silence, he said: "When walking until the water ends, sit and watch the clouds arise."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The autumn colors are desolate and clear; morning and evening grow ever cooler. One truly knows that the seasonal rhythms do not yield.
Those who study the Way among the groves eat when hungry and add clothing when cold, yet they do not realize that there is suffering and joy in the world.
But tell me, how does one come to know suffering and joy? He then said: "One only knows that affairs pass before one's eyes..."
Jue Lao came from above. Xing Daozhe returned after clearing the fields.
He ascended the hall and said: "For three years he toiled in vain, playing with mud and water; his trousers tucked up and his breeches rolled back, he again took up the plow.
Only when the granary is full and the rice harvested does he return to the monastery, leaving it to the Zen practitioners to beat their own bellies as they please. Now tell me, what is this beating?
"What is this? Is it meditation, or is it food? He then said, "It is like using the wind to fan a fire; not much effort is required.
Entering the hall for discourse, he said, "One drop less will not do; one drop more will not do. Tell me, in whose sphere does this matter lie?
After a long silence, he said, "Day after day the sun rises in the east; night after night the moon flows toward the west."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The written characters are of one kind; the spoken words are of one kind; the resonance and force are of one kind;
the principles and meanings are of one kind. Why, then, do you say, 'He has not yet arrived'? He then continued: "It is simply because the nostrils are turned downward."
The Recorded Sayings of Master Baiyun Yuan, Volume Two;
The Recorded Sayings of Master Baiyun Yuan, Volume Three;
Verses and Eulogies.

The World-Honored One pointed to heaven and pointed to earth, taking seven steps; releasing both and gathering both, he doubled his focus and poured it forth. Within the coffin, upon the brocade, he added yet more flowers;
even until this very day, he lets fall rain and dew.
Having already been thoroughly exposed by the King of Liang, Bodhidharma sat upright at Shaolin; his talk of a "special transmission outside the teachings" was but a deception—
how could he not recognize this very point?

The true likeness in the stupa beneath the Double Peak of the Fourth Patriarch sits majestically, towering for four hundred springs. Those who have seen or heard of him throughout past and present all look up with admiration;
yet none know who can truly understand how to observe their own bodies.

The Fifth Patriarch’s sacred authority was beyond the evaluation of his contemporaries; how could the secret transmission at Shuangfeng have been a hollow claim? His former incarnation had grown old and could no longer pass on the bowl;
only by returning to take shelter under the same tree did he finally inherit the lamp. The fame of his past planting of pine trees still resounds today; may all spirits repay their mother’s kindness.
What has increased? Nowadays, the winds of the patriarchal tradition pervade the land; it is simply because one has been able to select the right peg from among them.
Master Po-chang carried nothing but a single cloth bag; what strange thing could he have sought within it? When weary, he had his pillow; when departing, he took it with him.
There is no hindrance whatsoever. Sometimes he would open up in the bustling marketplace; for the most part, it was his own buying and selling.
"The True Eulogy of the Late Master Yangqi of Yuanzhou:
A pearl in the azure sea, a needle thrust into soft mud. The tiger roars and the dragon sings; the cock crows and the dog barks. This is Yangqi of the whole world."
How truly profound!

The *True Praise for the Preceptor under whom I received the Precepts at Donglin in Chaling, Hengzhou*, using the moon in the water as a metaphor, has already been numerous since ancient times. I am not like them; what is it that I now set forth? A hundred-foot [tall tree]...
Having once advanced to the tip of the staff, one step across the mountain stream bridge leaves not a trace of river or mountain. It is certainly not a journey; what journey could there be?
Xuan Sha and Baoshou—were you not their peers? To the east of Yanfeng, at the mouth of the Mi River, for thirty-three autumns, the Great Lion’s Roar resounded.
Unfolding and rolling up, it is already finished; as before, the Mi River flows empty.
River waters flow; the nine rivers are separated by several thousand li. The father has prominent tusks while the son has no teeth. In vain do they labor to pull each other’s ears;
a single burner of incense sends forth a wisp of smoke that soon rises with the pine wind.
I, Xie, Prefectural Commissioner of Nan’gang, have recently received a visit from you, Secretary of the Imperial Archives Yu.
Though our meeting has been infrequent, the intent of your inscribed verse is most intimate: “The carp on the tree opens its mouth and laughs;

the stone tortoise blinks its eyes and becomes a neighbor. I have recently heard that you have been appointed as Vice-Commissioner in Shan-nan County; surely you will discern the falsehoods of all quarters.
"True. Do not be surprised that this school finds it difficult to find companions; to play in the tide, one must be a man who plays in the tide. Again he replied:
"I thank you for informing me of my errors—error, error, error! The nostrils of the iron ox have long since been pierced. To use one's entire body as a mouth is still not sufficient."
The mind—how can one endure this state of being utterly without a place to go or rest? Walking upon the edge of a blade, running amidst great flames;
a gnat swallowing a golden-winged garuḍa—how many have reached this point with composure? With a shout he scatters the white clouds without opening his mouth;
you who know the sword, once it is withdrawn, must guard it well. Buddhas and patriarchs are but skilled hands at sweeping away; you must truly possess a needle beneath the blade.
A chisel. There is the needle-chisel. *Rārali*. To find an advantage is to lose the advantage.
Entrusted to Official Yang;
for ten years I have heard his name, Yang Cigong. His writings are capable of reviving our school’s tradition. Dividing three into six, add a little more.
My son, you have directly attained the golden crow turning crimson in the dead of night.

Between two compositions written in my chamber, along with their prefaces, there were times when I was free from affairs in the hermitage; then, a sudden impulse for verse would arise, whereby I attained the "borrowing-less" realization of the Arhats as I entered the flow.
"Transforming Objects. These two titles, though their literary form relies on the compositions of poets, derive their essential meaning from our own school;
thus they may be called "Mountain Verses. May those who understand me share in this view.
The Arhat does not rely on the dust of emotions;
I have emerged from it myself. What need is there for the world to know me? When the moon is fine, I invite guests; when flowers bloom, I compose verses.
In training disciples, I have morning rules; in refining my phrasing, I am diligent. I seem quite like one who is preoccupied with trifles, yet stubbornly I do not recognize that "other."
Navigating the flux of things and their principles—how can one afford to neglect this? Each meets its time and understands how to cry out: the swarm of frogs welcomes the rain with urgency;

the solitary monkey’s call is clear amidst the frost. One after another, what comes first and last? Vast and silent, their natures and dispositions differ. At Mount Lu, he loathed those who were intoxicated; his ailment lay in a lack of clarity.
Entrusting the matter of the ancestral seal at Shuangfeng to the patriarchal school involves much more than mere extraction; now that he has returned to the hermitage, what can be done?
One cannot help but laugh at how five times the patriarch’s seat was moved, yet there was never any core substance to it—only wandering Chan practitioners running about.
Answer: As for Mr.
Guo Gongfu hiding his person, he does not need to shrink his head; as for him concealing his traces, he does not need to withdraw his feet. The golden crow soars through the vast heavens at midnight;
the jade hare cannot catch up with it.
Entrusted to Wang Yuanfu of the Nine Rivers:
A single thought arises following the Chan mind; when shall we meet as we have planned? Amidst the sound of springs after midnight, and the mountain colors at the hour of sunset.
The wind comes cold from the distant ravines; the sky is long, and the birds descend slowly. This is clearly not something of the ears or eyes; it can only be known with you. Incidentally composed:
there are no flowers to offer when visiting Niutou. Amidst the misty, clear breezes of several hundred autumns, today, within the Longmen Hermitage—
Old age: sitting alone as before in the cold breeze.

Having lived among the white clouds since my first dwelling, I have returned to the white clouds to spend my final years, fulfilling my lifelong vow. The ancient house is low and exceptionally clear; ivy climbs the steps, increasing the wildness.
Prosperity! The murmuring stream encircles the monastery, increasing one’s leisurely sentiments. What prevents us from begging for alms to dispel the cold and heat?

Though we may be officials of high rank, there is little need for formal welcomes or farewells. Fellow practitioners need not ask again about the Patriarchs; I have already emptied my cloth bag for you.
Entrusting this to Elder Dufangyuan, I smile at myself:
my hand has not yet personally grasped the fishing wheel. Indolent upon the river, I have merely drifted along;
yet these past years I have not exerted a single ounce of mental or physical effort, and yet from time to time, a scaled dragon appears upon my hook.
The cowherd boy suddenly lets out a chaotic lowing from atop his ox; from this point on, it is difficult to restrain when such inspiration arises. Who cares if passersby cannot hear enough?
He lingers about, taking up his flute once more to play. Singing aloud whenever inspiration strikes—how could he force himself? Let the ox graze as it pleases.
The lashes of the whip are sparse; lifting his head, he does not allow the spring breeze to take notice. After the rain has passed, the grass by the stream grows lush again.

Upon the stream, as spring arrives, the grass grows lush once more. Donning the straw raincoat during moments that are half-rain and half-sunshine, the oxen lie at ease—some stretched out horizontally, others resting upright.
Over there they low with contentment; over here they bellow with joy.
Sent from Dahu to the Secretariat Official Chang, regarding his conduct and what he preserves:
those who are officials and yet act like commoners possess titles without substance; having a mouth is no better than being mute.
The heart of the noble gentleman is bright and clear. It is fitting that he dwells beneath the sun and moon.

Encountering spring, aging and illness arise—what need is there to inquire? How many throughout antiquity and today have idly drifted away! The eastern wind gradually loosens [the ice] before the eaves.
Frost. One year of rigorous cold has come to an end.
In response to Elder Xiaoxinghua:
"Mellow spring colors fill the gardens; the flowers are gathered, yet one only fears the sudden change to shade. With whom can these boundless sentiments be shared?"
It is said: For many days, Hanshan has been silent; he sends word to Elder Yong of Baoning that beneath White Lotus Peak, he spends his days in leisurely play.
How often he laughs at the former master for lacking a "gate on the crown of his head. When the inspiration arises, he seizes the opportunity to bring it forth on the path.
He rose. He should also laugh at me for entering a deep village.
"The pearl on the golden plate cannot be moved; it rolls and turns, difficult to stay still. After waiting for a long while, its circular radiance was as clear and still as dew.
The retribution lands are preeminent from beginning to end; it is as if everything were pre-arranged. Old matters may occasionally remain, yet the new sun will arrive before long.
At the fifth watch, the rooster faces the moon; throughout the four seasons, bamboo shoots grow amidst the moss. How wonderful that this is clearly explained—let the ducks listen to the thunder.

Entrusting the master of the Chan estate, Xian, with the tilling of the fields, the harvest of rice has doubled that of previous years. The transformations of heaven and earth are right before one's eyes;
let this old fellow indulge in his vigorous admiration. Do not transmit this dharma casually.

The voice of the cuckoo repeatedly cries, "It is better to return home. Yet those among the people who understand this are few. Before one's eyes, the spring mountains and spring waters are lush and green;
where else could one seek to forget all artifice?

To Chief Clerk Chen Shidao: You honor the profound principles; Master Zongmen values the subtle workings of the mind. When we raise our discourse, we all arrive at the same truth; when we join hands, we do not return as separate individuals.

The spring has passed yet the flowers remain in full bloom; the pond is formed but the moon has not yet shone. It is simply because those who have once arrived there find that not even a hair’s breadth deviates from the Way.

The staff produced by Heaven has a dragon-like form, utterly distinct; who would begrudge the nine-jointed cane of Qiongzhou? At times he walks idly through the weeds, startling the snake so that it cannot burrow deep enough.
Existence and non-existence are raised together;
the Way is fundamentally mindless, yet it is not simply "no-mind. You must directly distinguish between the intimate and the distant.

Those who possess even a hair’s breadth of a path to follow are all called outsiders to the gate. Practice values being mindless, yet one still requires the mind; it is just like form and shadow following one another.
We were close friends. Although one may hide oneself in the dark, how can one resist the golden crow that renews itself day by day?
As I see off the Abbot Yong back to Mingxī, I recall our parting by the river twelve years ago; it was only by chance that we met again to gaze at the snow on Lufeng Peak.
Tong. Liánqiáo’s expectation to enjoy the cool breeze was abruptly fulfilled (meeting Yuántōng in the winter of Xīnyǒu and returning to Wǔzǔ in the summer of Rényīn).

The water and rocks in the Gānlù Pavilion are extraordinary; what could one possibly do there from morning until evening? Having exhausted all the places where the ancients had not yet reached, he applied needle and chisel to each and every point from the beginning.
Whether there is benefit or no benefit, where the hand cannot reach, one strives to exert effort. It is perfectly round and seamless.
Forming two sides, he throws them to the ground; their golden sound is like that of tiles and rubble. There is damage, yet there is no damage.
How many times has he rolled in grass while still wearing his robes? From the treetops, pairs of fish are startled up; from atop the rocks, long bamboo shoots burst forth.

When asked, "Where do you intend to go with this staff upon your shoulder? he replies, "The great void conceals the tracks of birds. He advances, wishing to remain hidden, yet his words become ever more manifest. Directly!
Attaining the blue sky, a thunderclap resounds. A-he-he! Who can fully know it? The spring beneath the steps suddenly flows backward;
the white clouds atop the ridge dare not be white. The eye atop Yangqi’s head is not yet true; how could the eye behind Yangqi’s head be intimate?
At that time, there were three or five hundred at a single assembly; how many could truly penetrate the golden dust? You, sir, are about to depart for Jiangdong;
I have already retired in seclusion and need not concern myself. A pure breeze shall surely carry your good news here; look, as you stride alone toward the south, north, east, and west.
A fly piercing through a window, driven by its love for light, drills into the paper; how many hardships it endures where it cannot pass through!
Suddenly, it strikes the path it came upon, and only then realizes it has been deceived all along by its own eyes.
I stayed with the monk Jiujiang for one night before the lamp gazing at Mount Lu. In the blink of an eye, five years have passed since that time (when I came to Fahua).
Today, the white clouds are truly lovely to behold; they drift and unfurl while the waters flow on in a gentle murmur.

Examining the collected poems of Yang Cigong and the poems of the Master of Non-Action (Wuwei zi), they are both ancient and modern. Obscure at the beginning and clear at the end, they are difficult for people to perceive.
Not only do they correctly capture the essence of the *Guofeng* (Airs of the States), but they also branch out separately to communicate with the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Entrusted to Ling Jingwei, the Librarian;
as long as there is no deception, there will ultimately be one who understands. Pure and bright as the sun and moon, what need is there for constant face-to-face meetings?
White clouds in summer days;
summer days are most fitting for mountain temples. How much leisure and ease! In the quiet courtyard, fragrant grasses grow long; from the perilous ridges, scattered clouds pass by.
Cave waters flow far through the corridors; rock winds enter the hall in abundance. It is even more so on nights when the stars are few—the moonlight pierces through the pines and the vines.

The inspiration for this poem on white clouds and clear nights is entirely unsettled; at midnight, I am still far from sleep. The window is bright with snow outside the eaves; the chamber is still with the sound of a spring among the bamboos.
Several times I have reached the realm of silence, only to return once more to the presence of forms. As I lingered over these verses, I did not realize that the light of dawn had already spread.
Zizhen painted my portrait for Ningchen.
Because of this, I have shown that when the brushwork is mature, it becomes refined; it is vivid and lively, like the full moon on the fifteenth day.
Two nines make eighteen—since ancient times I have loved to chant "la la li," and when inspiration strikes, I add even more "du du du."
Seeing Chan practitioner Xuan off:

Within the shadow of the blade’s edge, the brow furrows; amidst the flash of a thunderclap, the smile opens. Ascending and descending at West Hermitage, he delivers beings throughout the ten directions;
having failed to pass through the Dragon Gate, he returns empty-handed.
In response to Mr. Feng, the scholar:
Vimalakīrti kept his mouth shut and traveled private paths; Old Pang spoke much and offended the Patriarch.
If you are a guest beneath the gate of Xianan, then every person before your eyes possesses the divine pupil.
Autumn rains, autumn rains;
the mountain air is cool. I long to add layers to my clothing, yet I do not know how these red dusts of the world can extinguish the stifling heat and humidity.
From the shallow stream, new sounds arise; the tall bamboos return to their former green. My sickly body has somewhat recovered, so that I may not neglect the instructions of Mañjuśrī.
The Mid-Autumn Moon:

Throughout the night of the Mid-Autumn Festival, the moon shines; dew falls like pearls across the entire forest. A gentle breeze rises, and as the clouds part, the myriad valleys reveal their distinct features.
In response to Imperial Censor Li’s *Feng rù sōng* (Wind Entering the Pines) lyric:

The zither has a melody called "Wind Entering the Pines. Truly hearing it, one perceives only what defies reason. A whistling sound fills the space between the seats; It is in the ear, yet not in the ear.
A Poem on Receiving a *Jǒng* Staff, Sent to the Chan Practitioner Neng:
Mount Sumeru rests within the eye, yet not a hair’s breadth of effort is expended. Lifting the nine-jointed *jǒng* staff, the sweat flows down the spine.
What was once heavy is now light; what was paired has become solitary. I present this to accompany your journey, standing tall amidst the spring colors.

On the ninth day, the chrysanthemums’ golden stamens cluster thickly, fresh with dew. Pluck them to brew tea and enjoy this auspicious morning. Why need one wait for the proper season to raise the cup?
Wine: It possesses only a fragrant aroma that intoxicates people of its own accord.

Sent to the Chan practitioner Tan to care for his parents—lofty and unknowable—is the pure wind filling the vast void. In the past, you yourself were in violation; one morning, you returned and felt remorse.

Thus, throughout these ten years, at every step we have been like the bird that pecks and the one that pries open the eggshell; in vain do you boast of traveling through a hundred cities—who understands how the feet shift in the dark?
In vain do you boast of opening the towers and pavilions—who can avoid being caught in the snare? Without cause you harbor grand sentiments, yet you end up becoming petty and narrow-minded.
Then I thought of my compassionate mother’s heart; though a thousand li away, it was not remote. Crawl-kneed, I gazed toward Guilin; winding along, I took leave of Mount Lu.
A single word escaped the mountain: “The staff of bracken grows dragon horns. He patted my shoulder, bidding me preserve myself well; in a turn of the hand, he left me alone.
Having firmly grasped it, he brings it forth again; then he points to the crane in the distant heavens.
*Duḥ!* Because of this matter, he instructs the Head Seat, Xiaoshan:
"The new bird’s song is truly fine. Suddenly I recall last night facing Xunlao. The red wheel [of the sun] is bright and radiant amidst the hundred flowers."
Incense. Limitless travelers tread upon the fragrant grasses.
Answering Master Yongzang:
the silkworm-eyebrowed maiden’s whiskers trail the ground; the scorched-tail donkey’s horns point to heaven. At noon, it is ridden into the marketplace.
Too late! How many nostrils have been pierced by him?
Sending forth the Elder Yanshou, there is no place to grasp;
the illness is difficult to remove. Letting go of the snake’s head, one strokes the tiger’s whiskers. Today, Shuangquan has opened a single path.
The pulse is clear; observe the long coral growing on the moonlit peaks.
Because of the snow, the jade-like flowers fill the empty mountains overnight. At dawn, all say it is a fine, cold snow; though each flake falls as it may, its nature is known.
Although we were at the dwelling, the circumstances still left us halfway there.
Movement coincided with events;
the rice was like pearls and the noodles like jade. Having finished eating, we walked along the stream for several bends when, suddenly, we encountered a man with a hoe.
The Old Man: "I myself sing aloud while others drum upon their bellies.

In response to the Zen guest’s words, "word after word," there is whirling wind and falling snow; in silence, "utterly silent," there is thunder crashing and lightning flashing within the pores of a lotus fiber.
Riding upon the Great Peng, he casually knocks down the moon from the edge of the heavens.
He declines the invitation for peace. To the Elder Yang, Grand Minister:
his heart of benevolence is beyond naming; over a thousand li, the ancient wind is pure. If this mountain monk could obtain white clouds...
Yin: Sitting upright and burning incense, I pass this life.
To send off Zen practitioner Ming:
cut the nails, sever the iron—whether resting or not; thread comes, thread goes—meeting or not meeting. In the solitary night, three thousand *li* away.
Proceeding, the golden crow flies up onto the coral tree. Entrusting this to my friend Hu Zhailang, who has long been parted from me;
I have taken up my staff and happened upon you by chance. When the Way is present, how could one begrudge material things? When the mechanism is profound, the mind is not discussed.

"You, my lord, cherish the continuity of generations; I myself delight in the depths of the clouds. Though our positions differ, the principle remains the same—yet I still feel ashamed before Zhi Daolin.

In his reply to the worldly scholar, he asked: 'Where has the white cloud ever come to rest? Upon the rock, amidst the pines, I have opened it once for you. It was specifically to discuss the ground of the mind."
Dharma. A clap of thunder under a clear blue sky and bright sun.
Inscription for the Memorial Pagoda of Master Yun’gai Hui and the Pagodas of the Five Peaks Patriarchs:
Our Patriarch occupies the center; the mountain ridges come from the east in perfect alignment. The luster of the stream flows away long and far.

The Sangha shifts the trees at the edge of the clouds; the guest offers incense by the seashore. From this point on, along the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers, the lingering influence shall stir Luoyang.
When the Chan master Ben presented his poem "Imitating the Clouds," I declined it; therefore, following its rhyme, I offer this verse in praise of the mountain.
To provide for the journey, the wind immediately spreads a dense shade; it sprinkles moisture upon a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. Do not say that this is merely a mindless wandering;
what kind of mind is this very "wandering"? *Du!* (Aha!)

Answer: An heir who does not dwell [in attachment] is as rare as a phoenix chick or a qilin cub from time immemorial. Though he may be called an auspicious omen or a blessing, he cannot yet be so designated.
Lately, due to the great snow, the white clouds have fallen; the entire mountain is filled with jade-like monkeys.
Entrusting this to the old mountains of Longmen, the ancestral succession remains unestablished.
When the pearl at the bottom of the sea moves, the moon reappears amidst the clouds; on a fine night without wild winds, the pure light is entirely one piece.
Ten Poems on Dwelling at Mount Fahu The mountain is so silent;
how can one discourse here? Having returned to seclusion, I have long been cut off from all strange news. How many seekers of the profound have come to visit me?
Piercing through the clouds, few fail to lose their way amidst the mists.
The cliff spring circles the thatched hall for long, its sound echoing; whenever midnight arrives, it becomes exceptionally clear. Its distant course naturally flows on and off;
who could boast of the skillful playing of a jade zither?

In the deep ravine, clouds disperse and the moon is once again full. Watching in stillness, the myriad waves shimmer and glisten. When the cold reflections coalesce, one does not notice their shifting;
suddenly, they circle and illuminate the peaks ahead.

The plum rain has not ceased for even ten days; now that the sun has come out, ten thousand miles of sky reveal a vast, clear azure. What need is there for further inspiration in this mountain pavilion?
As before, the emerald screens stand clearly arrayed.
In spring, the mountain streams turn green like moss; In autumn, the mountain maples glow red like fire. Throughout the year, few encounter such fine sights;
Truly, they are surpassed by my solitary cane.
A young child rides a cow across a wooden bridge; his head and horns stand out prominently amidst the perilous current. He walks and sings, speaking as if on level ground;
only through long practice can one attain such freedom.
Wild birds have long ceased to come, bearing blossoms in their beaks; in the secluded courtyard, nothing can defile the moss. It is crystalline and clear, resembling the hue of autumn waves;
those who approach it will undoubtedly find no ripples rising.
Hastening toward wealth, honor, and affection, filling their carriages and overflowing their carts as they travel day and night— yet when they look back at a single bowl and a single staff,
who would know that there is not much to choose between the two?
The monkey plucks fruit, fearing others will know; his eyes glance east and west while his hands move in secret. When viewed with a cool mind, it is truly laughable:
how can such a senseless creature act in this way?
Every time I see a monk returning from the summit, my heart cannot help but ache with weary sorrow.
When will you show me the place where you dwell, so that a thousand peaks may no longer feel the cold?
The Recorded Sayings of Master Baiyun Yuan, Volume Three;
The Recorded Sayings of Master Baiyun Yuan, Volume Four;
One Hundred and Ten Verses on Ancient Cases by Master Yuan of Fahuashan in Shuzhou.
Compiled by the junior disciple Chuning.
The World-Honored One ascends the seat:
His towering cranial mark is ultimately difficult to behold; When will his unfolding and rolling be like a flash of lightning? If that time were this time—
People say that when Mañjuśrī struck the gong, it was like threading a needle, and that when the World-Honored One held up the flower, everyone says it was the "holding-up-of-the-flower-and-smiling.
Yet they do not know how to discern the ancestral wind with this. If one says that the eye and the mind occur simultaneously—
Realization. One cannot avoid being dimly aware within a dream (Aha!).
When an outsider asked the Buddha:
"The ten-thousand-fathom cold pond is clear to its very bottom; the silvery fish, in the stillness of night, move toward the light. With a single pull of the rod, they follow the hook."
Above. The vast expanse of water scatters the bright moonlight.
Turn over the banner-pole before the gate.
Beyond the golden robe, what else is transmitted? The younger brother responds to the elder brother’s call—how could there be partiality? Turn over the banner-pole before the gate.
He departed, lest he be forced to remain leaning against the wall as before.
When Emperor Wu asked Bodhidharma about the primary truth of the holy dharma (*paramārtha-satya*), it was as if an arrow had already struck a vulture;
yet, with another arrow added, he was granted his pardon and returned directly to the peak of Shaoshi.
The Master sat. When the Prince of Liang ceased speaking and was about to leave, he called out [to him] (the Master said:
"Who wishes to be summoned?"). The Second Patriarch sought peace of mind;
from beginning to end, he searched for the mind but found nothing to be grasped. In the vast silence, no one of Shaolin could be seen; the old snow filling the courtyard was known once more.
Cold. Place the nostrils upon the upper lip as before.
Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha.
The great earth, mountains, and rivers are all jewels; to those who do not recognize them, they are but wild weeds. Sun-Face, Moon-Face—Buddha appears!
At that time, the shimmering light of coral shone brilliantly.
A monk asked Baizhang, "What is the extraordinary matter? Baizhang replied, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak."
The monks prostrated, and the Master struck them.
How could such great capacity and great function be in vain? Sitting alone atop the solitary peak is the exercise of expedient means (*upāya*);
were one to transmit the King’s decree even slightly erroneously, they would surely receive three thousand blows upon the crown of their heads.
Master Huangbo addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you here are nothing but fellows who eat the dregs of wine.
Traveling on pilgrimage like this, how could you have reached this day? Do you know that within the Great Tang Empire there are no Zen masters?
At that time, a monk came forward and said: "But as for those in various quarters who guide disciples and lead assemblies..."
"How is it? Baizhang said, "I do not say there is no Chan; I only say there is no teacher.
In the Great Tang Empire, there are no Chan masters. Let us take each other’s hands and return home.
He cast his hook intending to catch a black dragon, but who would have known he would catch a lame turtle?
Nanquan slaughtered the cat;
held up before the two halls, everyone saw it clearly. He raised his blade to seize the living *lilu* (tawny cat); alas, there was no blood beneath its skin.
It resulted in a corpse lying across the road.
Zhaozhou wears straw sandals upon his head;
at the stillness of night, the wildcat stretches itself wide. Reaching its paw over its head, its claws are revealed long.
Having patrolled within Wang Lao’s room, it hurries out in fear of the light of day.
Nanquan said: "People of this age see this single stalk of flowers as if in a dream.
Heaven and earth share the same root; it is naturally so. At that time, I was still glad to have met Nanquan, who pointed and said, 'Seeing these flowers is like a dream.
One must believe that within the alchemical elixir (the *hu* vessel) there is another heaven."
Zhaozhou’s “Qingzhou cloth robe weighs seven catties.
How difficult is it to carry a seven-catty robe? When the sun rises in the east, it is certain to set in the west. With one blow, the coral branch shatters to pieces;
thunder and hail roar through the mountains and streams.
Zhaozhou’s Interrogation of the Old Woman:
Amidst the chaos of war, he established the foundation of great peace; with clumps of rain and streaks of wind, it surpasses ancient times.
The old woman has thoroughly exposed you; few people know Zhaozhou’s true footprints.
A monk asked Dawsui, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder:
will this very thing be destroyed or not? Dawsui said, "It is destroyed. The monk said, "In that case, it follows along with it.
Dawsui said, "It follows along with it."
Whether it perishes or does not perish, the tongue has no bone; when it strikes the face, the eyes bulge out. The Great Companion still remains amidst the kalpa-fire;
the world is parched and tormented in vain clamor.
Linji’s three blows of the staff:
with one punch he toppled Yellow Crane Tower; with one kick he overturned Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, he adds more spirit;
where there is no elegance, he is nonetheless elegant.
Linji asked the monastery steward, "Where have you been? The steward replied, "I went to the city to sell yellow rice.
Linji said, "Have you sold it all? The steward said, "I have sold it all.
Linji drew a line across the ground with his staff and said, "Can you sell this too? The steward then shouted; Linji struck him.
Just then, the head cook arrived. Jì raised the previous conversation, and the cook said, "The Abbot does not understand the Master’s honorable intent.
Jì also struck the ground with his staff, making a single line, and asked, "And what about you?"
As he prostrates at the seat, [the Master] strikes him immediately.

A precious sword is brought forth, its blade like frost; how many times has it descended upon the battlefield to slay barbarian kings? Sentient beings and rational beings alike are cut into three pieces;
a single streak of cold light shoots beside the Dipper.
Linji addressed the assembly, saying: "Upon this ball of red flesh, there is a true person of no rank who enters and exits through the gate of your faces every day.
Those of you who have not yet realized this—look! Look! At that moment, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the true person of no rank?
Linji leaped down from his meditation seat, grabbed him by the chest, and pulled him close.
Dingqiseng said, "The Way, the Way. The monk remained silent. Jueyi pushed him away and said, "What kind of dried piece of excrement is this 'true person of no station'?"
The spring breeze sweeps vast and wide, warming heaven and earth; everywhere, the mountains are hidden within mists and vapors. The True Person of No Rank cannot be sought;
falling flowers are seen again as they follow the flowing stream.
Linji entrusted San-sheng, saying: "Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would be extinguished by this blind donkey?
Splitting open Mount Tai, the thunder is not so fierce; illuminating the vast ocean, the moonlight is not so bright. The blind donkey has extinguished the True Dharma.
"Eye! You have truly caused your mournful cries to shake the Great Tang.
Fengxue said, "If you establish even a single speck of dust, the state and its family will flourish, but the village elders will frown.
If you do not establish even a single speck of dust, the state and its family will perish, but the village elders will be at peace. The Master then took up his staff and struck once.
Downward, he returns them to their former places;

establishing the state, he still causes the rustic elders to rejoice. His majesty prevails beyond the borders without raising a speck of dust; his mastery of both civil and martial arts is unfathomable in its breadth and depth.
In this vast and boundless universe, how many such men are there?
A monk asked Sansheng, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Sansheng replied, "Stinking meat attracts flies.
Later, when Xinghua heard the monk recount this, he said, "I am not like that; it is a fly on the back of a donkey with a broken spine."
The spine-splitting flies are mostly stinking-flesh flies; who knows that Xinghua does not travel in vain?
Having long been accustomed to passing before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, he holds a golden halberd to celebrate the Great Peace.
Baoshou opens the hall;
the golden mallet comes down directly like a shooting star. A skilled hand catches it without wasting effort.
At that moment, it is cast into the surging waves—throughout ten thousand ages, there is no news of it.
A monk asked Shoushan, "When a student reaches the Jewel Mountain and returns empty-handed, what then?
Shoushan said, "A torch before every door.
"When returning empty-handed, who would believe it? A donkey carrying it and a horse laden with it enter the gate; every household raises its torch."
At midnight, the sky was as bright as day.
A monk asked Fenyang, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Fenyang replied, "A green silk fan provides sufficient cooling breeze."
A fan of blue silk provides sufficient breeze and coolness; only when one personally wields it can the madness be stilled.
One merely loves that which is perfectly round and seamless, yet before others, one’s eyes are as vacant as those of a sheep.
Master Yangqi asked Ciming, "When the dark birds warble their cries and leave the clouds to enter the jumbled peaks, what is it like?
Ciming replied, "I am walking through the wild weeds; you, moreover, have entered a deep village.
Yangqi said, "The official does not permit even a needle," and asked again for a question. Ciming then gave a shout. Yangqi said, "A fine shout! Ciming then—
"Hai! Qi also shouted "Hai! Minglian shouted twice. Qi then prostrated.
Carrying out the pearl from the dragon, he encounters a great merchant; as the golden tray is moved, its radiance remains. There is no need for a single word to discuss its high value;
taking each other by the hand, they return home to share many laughs.
Zhaozhou asked Touzi, "When one who has undergone the great death comes back to life, what is it like?
Touzi said, "Night travel is not permitted; at dawn, one must set out.
"Dead and then come alive, the teeth still bare—having reached the dawn, one must go on; who could have known he would arrive first? "In whose private villa is there a pond?"
[The Master] said, "On the back, a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be painted.
Emperor Tongguang said to Xinghua, "Since I brought the Central Plains under my rule, I have obtained a treasure."
No one had yet offered a price. Guanding said, "I request Your Majesty to examine this treasure. The Emperor opened it with both hands and saw that its head and feet were spread out.
Guanding said, "This is the treasure of a sovereign; who would dare to offer a price for it?"
The Prince of the Northern Tribes bends his bow to shoot; the General of the Southern Kingdom looks up to behold.
Upon the sands, nothing remains but a slanting shadow, as it flutters straight into the clouds above.
Master Liang-sui went to visit Magu. On his first visit, as soon as Magu saw him approaching, he shut the gate to his quarters.
On the following day, Liang-sui went up again, but Magu paid him no attention; instead, he took up a hoe and entered the garden.
On the next day, Liang-sui went up once more. When Magu saw him coming, he called out in a loud voice.
[The Master] said, "Liangsui. Liangsui responded, "Yes. Before the sound had even faded, he suddenly attained realization. He then said, "Preceptor, you must not deceive Liangsui.
Had I not come to see you, Preceptor, I would have been led astray for a lifetime by twelve volumes of sutras and treatises.
Thereupon, he returned to his own monastery, sold his house, and [established himself as a monk].
After concluding the lecture session, he gathered his fellow students and said: "What you all know, Liang-sui knows entirely;
what Liang-sui knows, you all do not know."
Shutting the door and taking up the hoe was already too late; now I must face you again and endure this confusion (chátú).
Having long realized within the light that I have been deceived, I finally believe there is no one with whom I can leave the household life.
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have heard that you, Master, personally met Nanquan—is this true?
Zhaozhou replied, "In Zhenzhou, we grow large radishes."
In Zhenzhou they produce large radish heads; I inform you that the place of origin must be clearly understood. Most patch-robed monks swallow them whole;
though they examine them closely, few obtain their true flavor.
Vimalakīrti asks Mañjuśrī about the Dharma-gate of non-duality.
One, two, a hundred thousand, ten million—counting on one's fingers, the numbers cannot be distinguished. For a moment, set them before a dark window;
tomorrow I shall calculate them with you once more.
The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* says: "When I do not see, why do you not see the place where I do not see?
If you see that 'not seeing,' it would naturally not be the characteristic of that 'not seeing.
If you do not see the ground of my not seeing, it would naturally not be a material thing; how could it not be you?"
The pillar before the hall has long been pregnant; at last it gives birth to a child, truly brilliant. Before he can even speak, he composes a rhapsody;
with a single stroke, he wins the title of Grand Marshal.

The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* states: "If a person is treated with contempt by others, it is because of the karmic offenses of that person’s previous lives which would have caused them to fall into the evil realms;
because they are now treated with contempt by people in this life, the karmic offenses of their previous lives are thereby extinguished."
Who does not know that water does not wash water? The whirlwind is ever still, yet it rushes on with great haste.
If one could truly employ the days of a thousand-year calendar, one would avoid being hauled up by the finger of the patrol officer.
He requested that Master Fu lecture on the sutras.
Yet when had the Master ever lectured on the sutras? Master Zhi used skillful means to assist him; with a single stroke, everything on the desk was rendered void of graspable substance.
This left even King Liang with eyes bulging in astonishment.
Longtan was originally a cake-maker from Jingzhou whose home was near Emperor Tiantai. Every day he would send ten fresh cakes to the Master Tiantai;
the Master would always set aside one cake, saying, "I bestow this upon you so that it may provide shade for your descendants.
This continued for many years until one day, the Emperor suddenly asked, "These cakes were brought by my disciple."
"Why do you instead say it is a gift? Your Imperial Majesty, you say this was brought by you; what fault is there in returning it to you?
The baker had a slight realization that ten cakes must each be returned one by one.
He pondered what it meant to "provide for one's descendants," and he took out the round cakes and brought them back again.
He entered [the monastery], yet he did not realize that the *amṛta* (clarified butter) had reached the crown of his head.
Longtan then went to Emperor Tianhuang to leave the household life. He spent three years reciting the scriptures. One day, he asked:
"Since I arrived here, I have not received any instruction from the Master regarding the essential point of the mind. The Emperor said to him: "You..."
When he brought the tea, I accepted it for you. When you paid your respects, I immediately bowed my head.
Where was the essential point of my mind not shown to you? Longtan stood there pondering. Huang said, "If you see, you see; if you try to conceive it, you are already mistaken.
At these words, Longtan attained a sudden and great awakening.
Leaving the white robe to join a master, one values the toil and hardship; offering tea and inquiring after one’s well-being—all performed with personal devotion.
To pointlessly recount the affairs of three years again would only make the street vendor selling cakes laugh to scorn.
Deshan was standing in attendance in Longtan’s room. Deep into the night, Longtan said, "Why do you not go out?
Deshan then said, "I take my leave," and pulled back the curtain. Seeing that it was dark outside, he said, "It is dark outside. Longtan said, "Come in."
He then rolled a paper candle and handed it to Shàn. Just as Shàn raised his hand toward the candle, Dàntán suddenly blew it out.
Shàn then prostrated himself. Dàntán asked, "Son, what principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself?
Shàn replied, "From this day forward, I shall no longer doubt the tongues of the old monks throughout the world."
Yantán said: "In the future, you shall build a thatched hut atop a solitary peak and go about scolding the Buddhas and reviling the Patriarchs.
The mutual subduing of light and darkness is not worth mentioning; to have even a hair’s breadth of understanding is not yet intimacy. When the paper lamp suddenly goes out, the eyes are revealed."
[He] went out. [The Master] smashed [the bowl], and there was not a single person left of the Great Tang.
Attendant Kuò asked Dēngshān, "Where have all the sages of antiquity gone?
Shān said, "What? What? Kuò said, "The Emperor himself has mounted his flying dragon horse; the lame tortoise goes forth."
"What are you doing with your head? Deshan then stopped. On the following day, while bathing, Deshan took a wooden mallet and struck the temple bell once.
As the bell-ringer turned his head, Deshan asked, "How was the case last night?"
Kuo said, "It is only today that this old man has finally glimpsed the truth.
When Yunpeng spreads its wings, the heavens lose their light; the frog at the bottom of the well vainly croaks 'du-du'. Suddenly the great sun turns and leaps forth;
a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks stand starkly bare."
When Xuefeng was staying at his hermitage, two monks came to pay their respects.
Upon seeing them approach, Xuefeng propped up the gate of the hermitage with his hand, leaned his body out, and said, "What is this? The monks also said, "What is this?
Xuefeng lowered his head and returned inside the hermitage. Later, the monks went to Yantou, who asked, "Where have you come from? The monks replied: [as above].
A monk from Lingnan arrived. Tou asked, "Have you been to Xuefeng? The monk replied, "I have.
Tou asked, "What words or phrases did he say? The monk recounted the previous conversation. Tou asked, "What did he say? The monk replied, "He was speechless;
he lowered his head and entered the hut. Tou said, "Alas! In the beginning, I regretted not telling him about the final word."
[The Master] said: "If one were to speak of it, no one in the world could withstand Old Xue. When a monk came at the end of summer to seek further instruction, the Master asked:
'Why did you not ask [before]? The monk replied: 'I did not dare to be casual. The Master said:
'Although Xuefeng was born on the same mat as me, he did not die on the same mat as me. If you wish to recognize the final word, simply..."
This is it. After Xuefeng retired into his hut, no one on the road could see him anymore. Fortunately, there was an old friend a thousand miles away.
They were of the same root and died at the same time, yet not at the same moment.
A monk asked Xuansha, "I am a student newly entered into this forest; I beg the Master to point out an entrance for me.
Xuansha said, "Do you hear the sound of the Yan River water? The monk said, "I hear it. Xuansha said, "Enter through here."
Heaven-born is this child from Kunlun with azure eyes; though his artistry surpasses that of others, he himself does not know it.
Time and again, when black winds overturn the great ocean, he emerges and submerges within the waves, sporting at ease.
Lingyun saw peach blossoms and awakened to the Way.
What was it like at Lingyun’s place of awakening? If one has not reached the ultimate, no one can discern it for them.
At the foot of Mount Hua throughout the ages, who knew that Pan Lang was riding backward on his donkey?
Qianfeng addressed the assembly, saying, "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance;
you must penetrate each one thoroughly before you can sit with ease. Yunmen stepped forward and asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not see what is outside the hermitage?
Qianfeng laughed heartily. Yunmen said, "This is still a matter of doubt for students."
At the dwelling, Feng asked, "What kind of mental activity is yours? The Gatekeeper said, "I also wish for the Master to understand thoroughly.
Feng said, "Only then can you sit securely.
The shopkeeper took brass to test the appraiser, saying, "It is difficult to find anything that resembles this true gold. The appraiser shook his sleeves and walked away first.
He departed. His face covered with shame and embarrassment, he did not dare to show anger.
Qianfeng addressed the assembly, saying: "If you raise one, you must not raise two;
to let one pass is to fall into the second. Yunmen stepped forward and said: "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went back to the South."
Yue departs. Feng says, "Today there shall be no communal labor. The gatekeeper then returns to the assembly.
Black and white are clearly distinguished across the full board; not a single move has been made in error. Pity the countless onlookers;
though the axe handle rots away, they remain entirely unaware.
A monk asked Yunmen, "If one kills one's father and mother, one repents before the Buddha;
but if one kills the Buddha and the Patriarchs, where does one repent? Yunmen said, "Exposed."

Stirring up soil and scattering dust, there was no place to take refuge; he pressed his body straight before the imperial palace tower. Turning his head, he could not see the path by which he had come;
below was the Yellow Springs, and above was Heaven.
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? Yunmen said, "Pervasive.
"Upon his crown he has truly come as one who is blind; Shining upon heaven and earth, yet not of the same time. Do not hold it aloft in the hands of Great Compassion;
Walking alone at night, who can know it?"
A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still any transgression? Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru.
Mount Sumeru fills the universe; even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes cannot see through it. Only one who can personally ride it backward may do so.
An ox: throughout its life, it never follows behind others.
A secular official asked Yunmen, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in water? Yunmen said, "In the clear waves, there is no path through.
The official asked, "From where did you, Master, obtain this? Yunmen said, "If you ask again, from where would it come?"
The Official asked, "What is it like when one goes forth in this very manner? The Gatekeeper said, "Layer upon layer of mountain passes.
Truly, the moon reflected in water is not difficult to grasp; It is simply that people of the present age do not personally engage with it. Master Shaoshi has brought it forth:
"Layer upon layer of mountain passes, yet its radiance is ever more new."
Yunmen said: "I grant you three blows of the staff.
To pierce the three barriers with a single arrow is not difficult; why do you still linger amidst right and wrong?
It is a pity to laboriously call forth this 'rice-bag'—only after three blows will you know the piercing cold to the very bone."
King Daewang invited National Master Naoshan to open the hall. Naoshan ascended the seat, gathered his saṃghāṭī robe, looked around to left and right, and then descended from the seat.
The Great King stepped forward, took hold of Naoshan’s hand, and said, "How is this assembly on Vulture Peak any different from today?
Naoshan replied, "I thought you were just a worldly man."
Flurries of snowflakes shine upon the heavens of Min; the Lord of Min rarely encounters such sights and is doubly delighted.
Once the spring breeze blows across the great earth, not a single flake remains before his steps.
A monk asked Dongshan, "What is the Buddha? Dongshan said, "Three pounds of flax.
The weight is clearly defined, not given to you; do not let the pupil in your eye grow angry.
Of the thirty-six thousand days in a hundred years, when you find a place of joy, simply rejoice.
Yangqi raised the words of Panshan, saying: "The one path leading upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
He then commented: "It is stuck on the mouth.
Panshan’s upward path—how mysterious! Rarely is one seen whose ears have been pierced. Since it is stuck on the mouth, there is nothing to bite.
Only in this state does one know that the thousand sages could not transmit it.
A monk asked Yangqi, "When one parts the clouds and sees the sun, what then? Yangqi said, "He who comes from the east shall sit in the east."
Yao and Shun let their robes hang as all nations pay homage; Pushing through the clouds to see the sun, there is no need for further words. Those who come from the East sit in the East;
Grasses and trees once more receive the freshness of dew and rain.
A monk asked Yangqi, "What is the Buddha? Yangqi said, "A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves.
"A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves; I report this to the traveler: open your eyes. If you see it within the weeds, you shall surely lose your life;
It is simply because its kicking and stamping are most distinct."
A monk asked Yangqi, "What was the meaning of Bodhidharma facing the wall at Shaolin? Yangqi said, "The man from the West did not understand the language of Tang.

Heaven is high and the earth is distant; it is not difficult to see. The waters are broad and the mountains are layered; it is not easy to discuss. Ten thousand ages, the eight winds cannot blow it away."
[The monk] entered. Since the people of the Western Heavens did not understand the language of Tang, a monk asked Yangqi:
"Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil. When a patch-robed monk attains the One, what can he do with it?
Yangqi replied: "The mouth of the alms bowl points toward heaven."
The bowl’s rim facing heaven at the hour of noon; a single mass of iron throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Sitting in silence against the wall at Shaolin for many years—this merely adds more grit to the eyes of the patch-robed monks.
Xiu Shan-zhu Wukong was traveling on pilgrimage when he entered Dizang’s Hall to take shelter from the rain.

While they were warming themselves by the fire and engaging in conversation, Dizang entered; seeing them, he asked, "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as you, Venerable, or are they different?
Xiu replied, "They are not different. Dizang held up two fingers and then departed.
Dizang stood at the vanguard and raised his finger; even now, the ancient masters have not yet glimpsed it. Heaven turns and earth revolves, yet it remains as casual as ever;
for ten thousand autumns and ten thousand springs, there are but two iron bars.
A monk asked Fayan: "Huishao asks the Master, 'What is the Buddha? Fayan said, "You are Huishao.
You have spent one large copper coin to buy a steamed rice cake; once you have eaten it into your belly, you will immediately be free from hunger."
A monk asked Fayan, "What is the student's own self? Fayan said, "The child of Bing and Ding comes seeking fire.
At the end, he weighed it once at eight *liang*, and then weighed it again until it was exactly half a *jin*. "Where does the zero-point of the scale lie? [he asked]. Who knows?
How strange it is to struggle over a mere hair’s breadth!
A monk asked Master Xuedou: "The mountain flowers bloom like brocade; the stream water is as clear as indigo.
Why is it that within the student's own sphere, one does not understand? Xuedou said: "Gazing with wide-open eyes from within a coffin. The monk...
If it is so, then one discerns the field from the sprouts, and recognizes the person through their words.
Xuedou said, "Thirty blows—wait for another time.
A single branch of withered grass forcibly conceals; a bright mirror facing the courtyard illuminates all that is hidden. With a face full of shame, he shifts his steps.
Depart! Its pure radiance is so brilliant that there is no way to avoid it.
Yun-gai Penglue visited Master Shuangquan Ya. Ya instructed him to contemplate the *śāla* tree (the "Banyan" or "Palace" tree), saying to the monks in his room:
"If you have a staff, I will give you a staff; if you have none..."
"Staff! I take away your staff! Although Yunpeng had observed this for a long time, he did not yet understand it.
One day, while Yunya was warming himself by the fire and Yunpeng was standing in attendance, Yunya looked at him and said:
"When you have a staff, I give you a staff; when you have no staff, I take it away from you."
The staff. As Baizhang was about to open his mouth, Xuedou stopped his hand and struck him with a pair of fire tongs.
Baizhang suddenly attained enlightenment.
Bestowing and taking away proceed together to verify the right and the wrong; as soon as one contends for the staff, one forgets the home. Suddenly, the iron mallet is like a whirlwind.
[The monk] arrived. He had lost the flowers before his eyes from before.
The monk requested further instruction from Master Langya: "The fundamental nature is pure and still;
why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Langya said: "The fundamental nature is pure and still; why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?"
Vastly profound and resonant, it has no front or back. When picked up, it sometimes becomes two pieces;
yet, if one simply returns to what was before, all will correspond, so as to avoid being spied upon by bystanders.
Master Xian of Beichen roasts a water buffalo on a winter night;
Taking its hide and horns, he seeks to outwit the mechanism. Laying it down, he gathers the remnants and returns home; Let the yellow snow fall as it will this time.
The whole family gathers around the fire, closing the purple gates.
Yanguan called to his attendant, "Bring me the rhinoceros fan.
The attendant said, "The rhinoceros fan is broken. Yanguan said, "The rhinoceros fan is broken; give me back the rhinoceros!"
Pitiable is this single rhinoceros-horn fan; In vain it is said that it has already been shattered. Boundless pure breezes follow wherever the hand goes;
Its towering presence stands out beyond the mundane world.
Mazu ascends the hall; Baizhang rolls up his mat.
Yesterday the east wind was suddenly fierce, and peach blossoms fell in profusion like red rain. Last night the east wind raged once more;
they fill the ground, yet one knows not where they have gone.
Master Pang asked Master Yangshan, "I have long heard of Yangshan; why is it that upon my arrival, you instead conceal [the truth]?
Yangshan held up his whisk. Master Pang said, "Exactly so. Yangshan asked, "Is this revealing or concealing?
Master Pang pointed to a pillar and said, "Though no one sees it, there is the pillar to bear witness."
Yangshan threw down his whisk and said: "Feel free to present this to all quarters.
Two eights make sixteen; even counting from the beginning, it is still not enough. He picks it up and scatters it in disarray before the steps:
everywhere on the ground, the spring moss is lush and green."
Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "On South Mountain there is a 'tortoise-nose snake'—the Elephant-Bone Tortoise-Snake stands across the great road.
Master Ling was regrettable for having lost his life; although Yunmen managed to bring it back to life, how can that compare to South Mountain, where there is no need for personal involvement?"
Shuilao went to visit Mazu. As he rose from his prostrations, intending to pose a question, Mazu gave him a kick that sent him tumbling over.

Shuilao attained sudden and great enlightenment. Rising up, he laughed heartily and said, "The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and the infinite subtle meanings are all realized by recognizing the source upon a single hair-tip. He then departed.
On a certain day at the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Ever since Master Ma gave that one kick, until this very day, the laughter has not ceased.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Baizhang Wulao let out a hearty laugh.
He then returned to his quarters.
A single kick that topples him is enough for a great laugh; all previous cleverness was but empty toil.
Even as a snake’s head requires heavy scratching, ten thousand myriad hairs emerge from a single pore.
A monk asked Touzi, "When you, Master, dwell on this mountain, what kind of realm do you experience?
Touzi said, "The horned girl has white hair;
the horned girl has white hair. Amidst a mass of fierce flames, flakes of snow fly. Who can truly dwell on a mountain like this?"
A Draft: Idle clouds and flowing waters do not return together.
The Patriarch’s Seamless Stupa—by whose hand was this seamless stupa fashioned?
Though there is a form, it is unfit for transmission; how can one forcibly write of that which has no tiers?
Grade. Forever suspended above the lapis lazuli palace.
Zhaozhou’s cypress tree:
a Korean hawk soars into the heavens. The dull-witted bird, rooted at the fence, does not fly away. Zhaozhou’s courtyard cypress—how [strange]!
"High! Who says the former master did not have these words?
A monk asked the Venerable Baoci of Tanzhou: "It is simply because the arising of emotion creates a barrier to wisdom, and conceptualization transforms the essence into something distinct.
But when emotion has not yet arisen, is there still a barrier? Baoci said, "There is. The monk said:
"Sentiment has not yet arisen; furthermore, what is there to separate them? Baoci said: "Du Chazhi, you have not yet met the right person.
Even without sentiment, they are still separated; how can you communicate? Between a hair's breadth, the paths are ten thousandfold. What a pity to run empty-handed at both ends."
This person was unable to see the essence of this school directly.
Nanquan went to visit Master Nirvana of Baizhang.
Baizhang asked, "Among all the sages of the past, is there any dharma that they have not preached for others? Nanquan replied, "There is. Baizhang asked, "How so?"

With gentle breezes filling the railing and a thousand trees in bloom, there is a spring distinct from that of heaven and earth.

Nan. A ball struck in swift water, blocking the mouth with a clod of earth.
The lotus of Zhimen.

At the location, one pace east and west, there was a branch opening.

water in the bucket.

Water. Before others, one must absolutely avoid being lacking in clarity.
A monk asked Wuzu Shiheshang, "What is the Buddha? Shiheshang replied, "Treading upon a scale-beam;
it is as hard as iron."
Treading upon the scale-beam, as hard as iron; at this moment, there is no reason that can be told.
A shooting star flies from the land of Silla, burning straight up toward the finger of Yunmen.
Zhaozhou washes his alms bowl;
the plum blossoms have fallen away and the apricot blooms unfold. One cannot avoid being touched by the spring breeze. The single breath speaks not, yet it contains all forms;
where could the myriad spirits go to thank it for its impartiality?
A monk asked Master Dayu Zhi, "What is the Buddha? Dayu said, "A saw cutting a scale-weight.
A saw cutting a scale-weight has no seams or cracks; it is blown by the wind and baked by the sun from morning until night. Although one is not permitted to make random conjectures about it.
[The Master] measured it; let it be weighed and carried around the world as you please.
Xuefeng said, "The Buddhas of the three periods turn the Great Dharma Wheel upon the flames.
Yunmen said, "The flames preach the Dharma for the Buddhas of the three periods, and the Buddhas of the three periods stand upon the ground and listen."
As the flames leap with radiant brilliance, he speaks most intimately; the boundless Buddhas draw near to hear him. Who would have known there was yet another bystander?
His nostrils reach toward the heavens—he takes no pleasure in you.
Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "The entire earth, gathered up, is as large as a single grain of millet;
he hurls it before you. You lacquer buckets do not understand—beat the drum for a communal viewing!"
Wandering the Southern Peak within the crevice of his eyebrows; drifting a fishing boat upon the heart of the great ocean. His meager art accompanies him and he never speaks of it;
let others beat their drums and watch without ceasing.
Guishan addressed the assembly, saying: "After I have passed away, I shall go to the house of a lay donor at the foot of the mountain and become a water buffalo.
On its left flank, I will write these words: 'The monk So-and-so of Guishan.'"
At this very moment, if you call him a monk of Mt. Huai, that is so; if you call him an ox, that is so.
I do not say he is Mt.
Huai, nor do I say he is an ox. Yet, where shall one discern his traces? To miss it by even a hair’s breadth is to lose the path upon which he came.
The road: for ten thousand kalpas there is no way to emerge from it.

Lingshu remained silent. He then raised this question for the Head Seat: "How can one attain [this]?"
A single turning word: it carves away at the stone stele above. The Head Seat says, "Not difficult. [The Master] provides the substitute response: "Teacher.
The single character "Teacher" is vast and towering; alone within the world, it settles right and wrong. In the end, water must flow toward the sea;
in the final analysis, clouds surely seek the mountain to return.
While Ciming was among the assembly, he went to Master Zhi’s quarters.
As Zhi sat there opening and closing his box and taking incense in his hand, intending to burn it, Ciming asked, "How do you burn it?"
Zhizhe then placed it in the incense burner and lit it. Ciming said, "That clumsy fellow has gone off in such a manner again.
Among thousands and tens of thousands walking the same path, how many move their bodies without moving a step? He picks up the incense burner right before one's face."
"Scorching! You rogue of a fellow, you go on like that!
Guishan sent a mirror to Yangshan. Upon receiving it, Yangshan took it up with both hands and held it aloft.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you say this is the mirror of Mount Tiantong, how can it be that it is in my hands?
If you say it is the mirror of Mount Yangshan, it was sent here by Mount Tiantong. Is there anyone who can definitively judge this?
The assembly remained silent. He then threw the mirror down.
The Master took up a mirror and presented it to the assembly; fools often compete over its beauty or flaws. Had he smashed it then and there, it could not have been sought after;
thus, he spared his descendants from having their hands defiled by it.

Familiarity. Without encountering the waves, one attains it.

"What is the Tathāgata’s speech? Changqing said, "How could a deaf person hear it?

It is said that the Tathāgata does not speak with double-tongued words. Three times three makes nine; this must be counted repeatedly. What deaf person could possibly hear such a dispute?
Even a fox-fur cloak cannot avoid eventually changing its master.
A monk asked Touzi, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there.

The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* says: "If one can transform objects, one is identical to the Tathāgata;
if one can transform objects, one is the Tathāgata. When spring comes, mountain flowers bloom everywhere;
naturally possessing a pair of hands for the destitute, one has never easily performed the *Santai* dance.

The hundred and ten verses on ancient cases from the *Fahua* [Lotus Sūtra] collection conclude here.

Dated the summer of the seventh year of the Jiayou era (Renyin), while residing in the West Hall of Wuzu. Because a Zen practitioner questioned me, I at that time used my own great matter as a seal for all [his questions].
However, many of these instances were not yet fully realized. I therefore wish to request further instruction on the karmic conditions of the ancient masters.

During that interval, as he gradually became more immersed [in the practice] and sought to realize its true nature, the Master granted him permission. At times, he composed verses for him, totaling more than thirty pieces.
In the ninth month of the autumn of the eighth year, the Gui-mao year, he resided on this mountain; as the mountains were deep and free from worldly affairs, he once again practiced as before.

Together they form one hundred and ten verses. Now, regarding this great matter, for one who has attained thorough realization, there is nothing that cannot be expressed through the skillful deployment of appearance and disappearance.
My only fear is that those on the path might either become mired in them or treat them with indifference, which would be a source of affliction.
If, however, one is gradually steeped in this and suddenly attains such realization, what remains for my verses to add? Thus, they are sublime, profound, and far-reaching.
If this brings about such a result, it would offer some consolation to those who have attained prior awakening.

If I may employ each according to their capacity, it would serve as a way to repay even a single hair’s breadth of the ancient sages’ vastness, like the oceans and mountains; this is my sole aspiration. Written at the end of the first month of summer in the year Jiachen (1064), during the reign of Zhiping.
